bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第185卷卷第一百八十五

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 185, the one hundred and eighty-fifth juan.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 185 (the one hundred and eighty-fifth juan).

sentences.zh: 【唐紀一】 起著雍攝提格正月，盡七月，不滿一年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 1] Beginning from the first month of the year Zhuanyong Shetige, through the seventh month, less than one full year.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records, Part 1] This section runs from the first month of the year Zhuanyong Shetige through the seventh month—less than a full year.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁未朔，隋恭帝詔唐王劍履上殿，贊拜不名。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day Dingwei, the first of the month, Emperor Gong of Sui issued an edict granting the Prince of Tang permission to wear sword and shoes in the palace hall and to be hailed in audience without having his name spoken.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (Dingwei), Emperor Gong of Sui decreed that the Prince of Tang might enter the hall wearing sword and shoes and be hailed in audience without having his name announced—the highest court honors.

sentences.zh: 唐王既克長安，以書諭諸郡縣，於是東自商洛，南盡巴、蜀，郡縣長吏及盜賊渠帥、氐羌酋長，爭遣子弟入見請降，有司復書，日以百數。

translations.literal: After the Prince of Tang had taken Chang'an, he sent letters to instruct the various commanderies and counties; thereupon, from Shangluo in the east to Ba and Shu in the south, prefectural and county officials, bandit chieftains, and Di and Qiang tribal leaders all vied to send their sons and younger brothers to present themselves and request surrender, and the responsible offices replied with letters numbering in the hundreds each day.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Prince of Tang had secured Chang'an, he sent proclamations to the commanderies and counties. From Shangluo in the east to Ba and Shu in the south, local magistrates, bandit leaders, and Di and Qiang chiefs rushed to send sons or younger kinsmen to court to submit; the civil offices answered with correspondence that ran to hundreds of letters a day.

sentences.zh: 王世充既得東都兵，進擊李密於洛北，敗之，遂屯鞏北。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong, having obtained the Eastern Capital's troops, advanced to attack Li Mi north of the Luo River, defeated him, and then encamped north of Gong.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Shichong secured the Eastern Capital's forces, he marched against Li Mi north of the Luo, routed him, and encamped north of Gong.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，世充命諸軍各造浮橋渡洛擊密，橋先成者先進，前後不一。

translations.literal: On the day Xinyou, Shichong ordered the various armies each to build pontoon bridges to cross the Luo and attack Mi; whichever bridge was completed first advanced first, so that front and rear were not coordinated.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinyou, Shichong ordered each army to build its own pontoon bridge across the Luo to strike at Mi. Whichever bridge was finished first crossed first, so the columns fell out of step with one another.

sentences.zh: 虎賁郎將王辯破密外柵，密營中驚擾，將潰；

translations.literal: The Tiger Guard commandant Wang Bian broke through Mi's outer palisade; Mi's camp was thrown into alarm and was on the verge of collapse;
translations.idiomatic: Tiger Guard commandant Wang Bian breached Li Mi's outer palisade, throwing Mi's camp into panic and bringing it to the brink of collapse;

sentences.zh: 世充不知，鳴角收眾，密因帥敢死士乘之，世充大敗，爭橋溺死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Shichong did not know of this and sounded the horn to recall his troops; Mi thereupon led his dare-to-die soldiers in a charge against them, and Shichong suffered a great defeat, with more than ten thousand drowned in the scramble for the bridges.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong did not realize what had happened and sounded the horn to rally his men. Mi seized the moment and led his shock troops in a counterattack. Shichong was routed, and more than ten thousand men drowned fighting for the bridges.

sentences.zh: 王辯死，世充僅自免，洛北諸軍皆潰。

translations.literal: Wang Bian was killed; Shichong barely escaped with his life, and all the armies north of the Luo were routed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bian was killed. Shichong barely escaped alive, and every army north of the Luo collapsed in flight.

sentences.zh: 世充不敢入東都，北趣河陽。

translations.literal: Shichong dared not enter the Eastern Capital and fled north toward Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong dared not return to the Eastern Capital and fled north toward Heyang.

sentences.zh: 是夜，疾風寒雨，軍士涉水沾濕，道路凍死者又以萬數。

translations.literal: That night there were fierce winds and cold rain; the soldiers waded through water and were soaked through, and those who froze to death on the road numbered yet another ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: That night a bitter wind and driving rain struck. Soldiers waded through water until they were soaked, and another ten thousand or so froze to death along the roads.

sentences.zh: 世充獨與數千人至河陽，自繫獄請罪，越王侗遣使赦之，召還東都，賜金帛、美女以安其意。

translations.literal: Shichong arrived at Heyang with only a few thousand men, bound himself in prison to request punishment; the Prince of Yue, Yang Tong, sent envoys to pardon him, summoned him back to the Eastern Capital, and bestowed gold, silk, and beautiful women to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong reached Heyang with only a few thousand followers, put himself in bonds to plead for punishment, and was pardoned by envoys from the Prince of Yue, Yang Tong, who then recalled him to the Eastern Capital and lavished gold, silk, and concubines on him to win him back.

sentences.zh: 世充收合亡散，得萬餘人，屯含嘉城，不敢復出。

translations.literal: Shichong gathered the scattered survivors and mustered more than ten thousand men, encamped at Hanjia City, and dared not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong rallied the fugitives until he had more than ten thousand men, encamped at Hanjia City, and did not dare venture out again.

sentences.zh: 密乘勝進據金墉城，修其門堞、廬舍而居之，鉦鼓之聲，聞於東都；

translations.literal: Mi pressed his victory, advanced to occupy Jinyong City, repaired its gates, battlements, and lodges, and took up residence there; the sound of gongs and drums was heard in the Eastern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: Following up his victory, Mi advanced to seize Jinyong City, repaired its gates, walls, and quarters, and made it his headquarters; the clang of gongs and drums carried as far as the Eastern Capital;

sentences.zh: 未幾，擁兵三十餘萬，陳於北邙，南逼上春門。

translations.literal: Before long he had more than three hundred thousand troops, arrayed them on Mount Beimang, and pressed south against Shangchun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he had massed more than three hundred thousand men on Mount Beimang, pressing south against Shangchun Gate.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，金紫光祿大夫段達、民部尚書韋津出兵拒之。

translations.literal: On the day Yichou, the Grandee of Splendid Happiness Duan Da and Minister of the People Wei Jin led troops out to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yichou, Grandee of Splendid Happiness Duan Da and Minister of the People Wei Jin marched out to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 達望見密兵盛，懼而先還。

translations.literal: Duan, seeing Mi's forces were numerous, was afraid and withdrew first.
translations.idiomatic: Duan, seeing how vast Mi's host was, took fright and retreated first.

sentences.zh: 密縱兵乘之，軍遂潰，韋津死。

translations.literal: Mi unleashed his troops to pursue; the army thereupon collapsed, and Wei Jin was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Mi sent his troops in pursuit; the army broke and fled, and Wei Jin was killed.

sentences.zh: 於是偃師、柏谷及河陽都尉獨孤武都、檢校河內郡丞柳燮、職方郎柳續等各舉所部降於密。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yanshi, Baigu, Heyang commandant Dugu Wudu, acting prefect of Henei commandery Liu Xie, Bureau of Appointments attendant Liu Xu, and others each led their jurisdictions in surrender to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi, Baigu, Heyang commandant Dugu Wudu, acting Henei prefect Liu Xie, Bureau of Appointments attendant Liu Xu, and others then brought their districts over to Mi.

sentences.zh: 竇建德、朱粲、孟海公、徐圓朗等並遣使奉表勸進，密官屬裴仁基等亦上表請正位號，密曰：「東都未平，不可議此。」

translations.literal: Dou Jiande, Zhu Can, Meng Haigong, Xu Yuanlang, and others all sent envoys with memorials urging him to take the throne; Mi's officials such as Pei Renji also submitted memorials asking him to assume the proper title and rank. Mi said: "The Eastern Capital is not yet pacified; this matter cannot be discussed."
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande, Zhu Can, Meng Haigong, Xu Yuanlang, and others all sent envoys urging him to ascend the throne, and Mi's own officials, including Pei Renji, petitioned that he assume imperial title. Mi replied, "The Eastern Capital is not yet taken; we cannot discuss this yet."

sentences.zh: 戊辰，唐王以世子建成為左元帥，秦公世民為右元帥，督諸軍十餘萬人救東都。

translations.literal: On the day Wuchen, the Prince of Tang appointed his heir apparent Jiancheng as left supreme commander and the Duke of Qin Shimin as right supreme commander, to supervise an army of more than one hundred thousand men to relieve the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuchen, the Prince of Tang named his heir Li Jiancheng left supreme commander and the Duke of Qin, Li Shimin, right supreme commander, and sent them at the head of more than one hundred thousand troops to relieve the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 東都乏食，太府卿元文都等募守城不食公糧者進散官二品，於是商賈執象而朝者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital was short of food; Grand Steward Yuan Wendu and others recruited those who would defend the city without consuming government grain and promoted them to honorary second rank; thereupon merchants bearing ivory tokens attending court became too numerous to count.
translations.idiomatic: Food ran short in the Eastern Capital. Grand Steward Yuan Wendu and others offered honorary second rank to anyone who would man the walls without drawing government rations. Merchants bearing ivory tally-sticks flocked to court in numbers beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 二月，己卯，唐王遣太常卿鄭元璹將兵出商洛，徇南陽，左領軍府司馬安陸馬元規徇安陸及荊、襄。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day Jimao, the Prince of Tang sent Director of Ceremonies Zheng Yuansui to lead troops out through Shangluo to subdue Nanyang, and Left Army Guard adjutant Ma Yuangui of Anlu to subdue Anlu and Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day Jimao, the Prince of Tang dispatched Director of Ceremonies Zheng Yuansui through Shangluo to reduce Nanyang, and Left Army Guard adjutant Ma Yuangui of Anlu to reduce Anlu and the Jing and Xiang regions.

sentences.zh: 李密遣房彥藻、鄭頲等東出黎陽，分道招慰州縣。

translations.literal: Li Mi sent Fang Yanzao, Zheng Ting, and others east out of Liyang by separate routes to summon and reassure the commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi sent Fang Yanzao, Zheng Ting, and others east from Liyang along separate routes to win over the commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 以梁郡太守楊汪為上柱國、宋州總管，又以手書與之曰：「昔在雍丘，曾相追捕，射鉤斬袂，不敢庶幾。」

translations.literal: He appointed Liang commandery prefect Yang Wang as supreme pillar of state and Songzhou commander-in-chief, and also wrote him a personal letter saying: "Long ago at Yongqiu we pursued one another; though one shot an arrow through a hook and cut off a sleeve, I dare not aspire to such magnanimity."
translations.idiomatic: He named Liang commandery prefect Yang Wang supreme pillar of state and Songzhou commander-in-chief, and wrote him personally: "At Yongqiu we once hunted each other down. Even if one of us had shot through a hook or cut off a sleeve, I would not presume to match the magnanimity of Duke Huan toward Guan Zhong."

sentences.zh: 汪遣使往來通意，密亦羈縻待之。

translations.literal: Wang sent envoys back and forth to communicate his intentions, and Mi also kept him on a loose rein.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wang exchanged envoys to signal his goodwill, and Mi treated him with a loose, conciliatory hand.

sentences.zh: 彥藻以書招竇建德，使來見密。

translations.literal: Yanzao sent a letter summoning Dou Jiande to come and see Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzao wrote to Dou Jiande inviting him to come pay his respects to Mi.

sentences.zh: 建德復書，卑辭厚禮，托以羅藝南侵，請捍御北垂。

translations.literal: Jiande replied with humble words and lavish gifts, pleading that Luo Yi was invading from the south and asking permission to defend the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande answered with humble language and rich gifts, citing Luo Yi's southern incursions as his excuse and asking leave to hold the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 彥藻還，至衛州，賊帥王德仁邀殺之。

translations.literal: Yanzao was returning when, at Weizhou, the bandit chief Wang Deren waylaid and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, Yanzao reached Weizhou, where bandit chief Wang Deren ambushed and killed him.

sentences.zh: 德仁有眾數萬，據林慮山，四出抄掠，為數州之患。

translations.literal: Deren had a following of tens of thousands, held Mount Linlü, raided in all directions, and was a scourge to several commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Deren commanded tens of thousands of men from Mount Linlü, raiding in every direction and plaguing several commanderies.

sentences.zh: 三月，己酉，以齊公元吉為鎮北將軍、太原道行軍元帥、都督十五郡諸軍事，聽以便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day Jiyou, the Prince of Tang appointed the Prince of Qi Yuanji as general who pacifies the north, supreme commander on the Taiyuan campaign route, and commander-in-chief of military affairs in fifteen commanderies, with authority to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day Jiyou, the Prince of Tang named the Prince of Qi, Li Yuanji, general who pacifies the north and supreme commander on the Taiyuan route, giving him authority over fifteen commanderies and leave to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝至江都，荒淫益甚，宮中為百餘房，各盛供張，實以美人，日令一房為主人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang of Sui reached Jiangdu, his debauchery grew still worse; within the palace more than a hundred chambers were prepared, each lavishly furnished and stocked with beautiful women, and each day one chamber was made host for the revels.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang of Sui reached Jiangdu, his debauchery only deepened. He had more than a hundred chambers in the palace lavishly furnished and filled with beautiful women, and each day a different chamber served as the seat of the revels.

sentences.zh: 江都郡丞趙元楷掌供酒饌，帝與蕭后及幸姬歷就宴飲，酒卮不離口，從姬千餘人亦常醉。

translations.literal: Jiangdu commandery aide Zhao Yuankai was in charge of supplying wine and food; the Emperor, with Empress Xiao and his favored consorts, went from feast to feast, cup never leaving his lips, and more than a thousand attendant consorts were likewise often drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangdu commandery aide Zhao Yuankai managed the wine and viands. The Emperor, Empress Xiao, and his favored consorts moved from one feast to the next, cup always at his lips, while more than a thousand attendant ladies were usually drunk as well.

sentences.zh: 然帝見天下危亂，意亦擾擾不自安，退朝則幅巾短衣，策杖步游，遍歷台館，非夜不止，汲汲顧景，唯恐不足。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor, seeing the realm in peril, was likewise restless and ill at ease; after court he would wear a headcloth and short coat, lean on a staff, and walk about, visiting every terrace and lodge, not stopping until night, anxiously glancing at the light as though he feared it would not last.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with the empire crumbling around him, the Emperor grew restless and uneasy. After court he would don plain headcloth and short coat, take up a staff, and wander every terrace and lodge in the palace until nightfall, glancing anxiously at the daylight as though afraid it would run out.

sentences.zh: 帝自曉占候卜相，好為吳語；

translations.literal: The Emperor himself understood astrology, divination, and physiognomy, and liked to speak in Wu dialect;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was versed in astrology, divination, and physiognomy, and liked to speak in the Wu dialect;

sentences.zh: 常夜置酒，仰視天文，謂蕭后曰：「外間大有人圖儂，然儂不失為長城公，卿不失為沈後，且共樂飲耳！」

translations.literal: He often set out wine at night, looked up at the heavens, and said to Empress Xiao: "Out there many people are plotting against me, yet I shall still end as Duke of the Great Wall, and you as Empress Shen—so let us drink and be merry!"
translations.idiomatic: He often held night banquets, gazed up at the stars, and told Empress Xiao, "Many out there are plotting against me, yet I shall still end as Duke of the Great Wall and you as Empress Shen—so let us drink and enjoy ourselves!"

sentences.zh: 因引滿沉醉。

translations.literal: He thereupon drained his cup and sank into drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: With that he drained his cup and fell deep into drink.

sentences.zh: 又嘗引鏡自照，顧謂蕭后曰：「好頭頸，誰當斫之？」

translations.literal: On another occasion he took up a mirror to look at himself and, turning to Empress Xiao, said: "Such a fine neck—who will be the one to cut it off?"
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he held up a mirror, studied himself, and said to Empress Xiao, "Such a fine neck—who will be the one to strike it off?"

sentences.zh: 后驚問故，帝笑曰：「貴賤苦樂，更迭為之，亦復何傷！」

translations.literal: The Empress asked in alarm the reason; the Emperor laughed and said: "Noble and base, suffering and joy, take turns in their turn—what harm is there in that!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress asked in alarm what he meant. The Emperor laughed and said, "High and low, joy and sorrow—they take turns. What is there to grieve over?"

sentences.zh: 帝見中原已亂，無心北歸，欲都丹楊，保據江東，命群臣廷議之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, seeing that the Central Plains were already in turmoil, had no heart to return north; he wished to make Danyang his capital, hold the lower Yangtze region, and ordered the ministers to debate the matter in court.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Central Plains in chaos, the Emperor had no wish to return north. He wanted to establish his capital at Danyang and hold the lower Yangtze, and ordered a full court debate on the plan.

sentences.zh: 內史侍郎虞世基等皆以為善；

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat vice director Yu Shiji and others all deemed it good;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat vice director Yu Shiji and others all approved the idea;

sentences.zh: 右候衛大將軍李才極陳不可，請車駕還長安，與世基忿爭而出。

translations.literal: Right guard general Li Cai strongly argued against it and begged the imperial carriage to return to Chang'an; he quarreled angrily with Shiji and left.
translations.idiomatic: Right guard general Li Cai argued vehemently against the move and pleaded for the court to return to Chang'an. He quarreled heatedly with Shiji and stormed out.

sentences.zh: 門下錄事衡水李桐客曰：「江東卑濕，土地險狹，內奉萬乘，外給三軍，民不堪命，恐亦將散亂耳。」

translations.literal: Chancellery clerk Li Tongke of Hengshui said: "The lower Yangtze is low-lying and damp, the land narrow and perilous; within it must support the Son of Heaven, without it must supply the three armies—the people cannot bear the burden, and I fear they too will soon scatter in disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellery clerk Li Tongke of Hengshui said, "The lower Yangtze is low, damp, and cramped. To support the Son of Heaven within and supply three armies without will crush the people; I fear they too will soon break apart in disorder."

sentences.zh: 御史劾桐客謗毀朝政。

translations.literal: The censorate impeached Tongke for slandering the court.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate impeached Tongke for maligning the government.

sentences.zh: 於是公卿皆阿意言：「江東之民望幸已久，陛下過江，撫而臨之，此大禹之事也。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the high officials all flattered him, saying: "The people of the lower Yangtze have long awaited Your Majesty's grace; when Your Majesty crosses the river to comfort and rule them, this will be the work of Great Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the high officials all chimed in: "The people of the lower Yangtze have long awaited Your Majesty. When you cross the river to comfort and rule them, you will be doing the work of Great Yu himself."

sentences.zh: 乃命治丹楊宮，將徙都之。

translations.literal: He then ordered the Danyang palace repaired and prepared to move the capital there.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Danyang palace restored and prepared to transfer the capital there.

sentences.zh: 時江都糧盡，從駕驍果多關中人，久客思鄉里，見帝無西意，多謀叛歸。

translations.literal: At that time grain in Jiangdu was exhausted; many of the elite guard who accompanied the court were men from within the passes, long absent from home and yearning for their native places; seeing the Emperor had no intention of going west, many plotted to rebel and return.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jiangdu was out of grain. Many of the elite guards who had followed the court were men from Guanzhong, long away from home and homesick. Seeing that the Emperor had no intention of returning west, many plotted to desert and go home.

sentences.zh: 郎將竇賢遂帥所部西走，帝遣騎追斬之，而亡者猶不止，帝患之。

translations.literal: Commandant Dou Xian then led his unit west in flight; the Emperor sent cavalry in pursuit to behead him, yet deserters still did not cease, and the Emperor was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Dou Xian led his men west in flight. The Emperor sent cavalry to run him down and execute him, but desertions continued, and the Emperor grew deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 虎賁郎將扶風司馬德戡素有寵於帝，帝使領驍果屯於東城，德戡與所善虎賁郎將元禮、直閣裴虔通謀曰：「今驍果人人欲亡，我欲言之，恐先事受誅；

translations.literal: Tiger Guard commandant Sima Dekan of Fufeng had long enjoyed the Emperor's favor; the Emperor had him lead the elite guard encamped in the eastern city. Dekan plotted with his friends, Tiger Guard commandant Yuan Li and palace attendant Pei Qiantong, saying: "Now every man of the elite guard wants to flee; if I speak of it, I fear I shall be executed before the matter comes to light;
translations.idiomatic: Tiger Guard commandant Sima Dekan of Fufeng had long been a favorite of the Emperor, who put him in command of the elite guard encamped in the eastern city. Dekan conspired with his friends Tiger Guard commandant Yuan Li and palace attendant Pei Qiantong. "Every man of the guard wants to run," he said. "If I report it, I may be killed before anything is done;

sentences.zh: 不言，於後事發，亦不免族滅，奈何？

translations.literal: if I do not speak, when the affair breaks out later I likewise cannot escape extermination of my clan—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: If I keep silent and it breaks out later, my whole clan will still be wiped out. What can we do?

sentences.zh: 又聞關內淪沒，李孝常以華陰叛，上囚其二弟，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard that within the passes has fallen, Li Xiaochang rebelled at Huayin, and the sovereign has imprisoned his two younger brothers and intends to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that Guanzhong has fallen, that Li Xiaochang rebelled at Huayin, and that the Emperor has imprisoned his two younger brothers and means to kill them.

sentences.zh: 我輩家屬皆在西，能無此慮乎？」

translations.literal: Our families are all in the west—can we be without such anxieties?"
translations.idiomatic: Our families are all back west—how can we not worry about the same thing?"

sentences.zh: 二人皆懼，曰：「然計將安出？」

translations.literal: Both men were afraid and said: "It is so—but what plan can we devise?"
translations.idiomatic: Both men were frightened. "True," they said, "but what plan do you have?"

sentences.zh: 德戡曰：「驍果若亡，不若與之俱去。」

translations.literal: Dekan said: "If the elite guard are going to flee, we had better flee with them."
translations.idiomatic: Dekan said, "If the guard is going to run, we had better run with them."

sentences.zh: 二人皆曰：「善！」

translations.literal: Both said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: Both said, "Agreed!"

sentences.zh: 因轉相招引，內史舍人元敏、虎牙郎將趙行樞、鷹揚郎將孟秉、符璽郎李覆、牛方裕、直長許弘仁、薛世良、城門郎唐奉義、醫正張愷、勳士楊士覽等皆與之同謀，日夜相結約，於廣座明論叛計，無所畏避。

translations.literal: They thereupon recruited one another in turn: Palace Secretariat attendant Yuan Min, Tiger Tusk commandant Zhao Xingshu, Hawk Raising commandant Meng Bing, seal keeper Li Fu, Niu Fangyu, chief clerk Xu Hongren, Xue Shiliang, gate officer Tang Fengyi, court physician Zhang Kai, merit officer Yang Shilan, and others all joined the plot; day and night they bound themselves together, openly discussing rebellion in public gatherings, without fear or concealment.
translations.idiomatic: They began recruiting others: Palace Secretariat attendant Yuan Min, Tiger Tusk commandant Zhao Xingshu, Hawk Raising commandant Meng Bing, seal keeper Li Fu, Niu Fangyu, chief clerk Xu Hongren, Xue Shiliang, gate officer Tang Fengyi, court physician Zhang Kai, merit officer Yang Shilan, and more. Day and night they swore one another to the plot and openly discussed rebellion in public, without the least concealment.

sentences.zh: 有宮人白蕭后曰：「外間人人欲反。」

translations.literal: A palace woman reported to Empress Xiao: "Out there everyone wants to rebel."
translations.idiomatic: A palace woman told Empress Xiao, "Everyone outside is plotting rebellion."

sentences.zh: 后曰：「任汝奏之。」

translations.literal: The Empress said: "You may report it as you please."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said, "Go ahead and report it if you wish."

sentences.zh: 宮人言於帝，帝大怒，以為非所宜言，斬之。

translations.literal: The palace woman told the Emperor; the Emperor was greatly enraged, deemed it speech that ought not to be spoken, and had her beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The woman told the Emperor. He flew into a rage, judged the report improper, and had her beheaded.

sentences.zh: 其後宮人復白后，后曰：「天下事一朝至此，無可救者，何用言之！

translations.literal: Afterward another palace woman again reported to the Empress; the Empress said: "Affairs of the realm have come to this in a single morning—there is nothing that can save them; what use is there in speaking of it!
translations.idiomatic: Later another palace woman reported to the Empress again. The Empress said, "The realm has come to this in a single morning. Nothing can save it now—why speak of it?

sentences.zh: 徒令帝憂耳！」

translations.literal: It would only add to the Emperor's distress!"
translations.idiomatic: You would only add to the Emperor's grief!"

sentences.zh: 自是無復言者。

translations.literal: From then on no one spoke of it again.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no one spoke of it again.

sentences.zh: 趙行樞與將作少監宇文智及素厚，楊士覽，智及之甥也，二人以謀告智及，智及大喜。

translations.literal: Zhao Xingshu was on close terms with Vice Director of Imperial Works Yuwen Zhiji; Yang Shilan was Zhiji's nephew. The two men told Zhiji of the plot, and Zhiji was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xingshu was close to Vice Director of Imperial Works Yuwen Zhiji, and Yang Shilan was Zhiji's nephew. The two confided the plot to Zhiji, who was delighted.

sentences.zh: 德戡等期以三月望日結黨西遁，智及曰：「主上雖無道，威令尚行，卿等亡去，正如竇賢取死耳。

translations.literal: Dekan and the others had set the fifteenth day of the third month to band together and flee west. Zhiji said: "Although the sovereign is without the Way, his authority and commands still hold sway; if you flee, you will meet death just as Dou Xian did.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan and the others had fixed the full moon of the third month to band together and flee west. Zhiji said, "The Emperor may be wicked, but his authority still holds. If you run, you will die like Dou Xian.

sentences.zh: 今天實喪隋，英雄並起，同心叛者已數萬人，因行大事，此帝王之業也。」

translations.literal: Now Heaven has truly abandoned Sui; heroes rise together; those of one mind in rebellion already number tens of thousands—seize the moment for a great deed, and this is the enterprise of an emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has abandoned Sui. Heroes are rising everywhere, and tens of thousands are already of one mind to rebel. Strike now and you will be founding an imperial enterprise."

sentences.zh: 德戡等然之。

translations.literal: Dekan and the others agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 行樞、薛世良請以智及兄右屯衛將軍許公化及為主，結約既定，乃告化及。

translations.literal: Xingshu and Xue Shiliang asked that Zhiji's elder brother, Right Army Guard general the Duke of Xu, Yuwen Huaji, be made leader; once the pact was settled, they informed Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshu and Xue Shiliang proposed Zhiji's elder brother, Right Army Guard general the Duke of Xu, Yuwen Huaji, as leader. Once the pact was sealed, they told Huaji.

sentences.zh: 化及性駑怯，聞之，變色流汗，既而從之。

translations.literal: Huaji was by nature dull and timid; on hearing this he changed color and broke into a sweat, yet afterward he went along with it.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji was dull and timid by nature. When he heard the plan he turned pale and broke into a sweat, but in the end he went along.

sentences.zh: 德戡使許弘仁、張愷入備身府，告所識者云：「陛下聞驍果欲叛，多醞毒酒，欲因享會，盡鴆殺之，獨與南人留此。」

translations.literal: Dekan sent Xu Hongren and Zhang Kai into the personal guard headquarters to tell those they knew: "The Emperor has heard that the elite guard wish to rebel; he has brewed much poisoned wine and intends, at a feast, to kill them all with poison, keeping only the southerners here."
translations.idiomatic: Dekan sent Xu Hongren and Zhang Kai into the personal guard headquarters to spread word among their acquaintances: "The Emperor has heard the elite guard mean to rebel. He has brewed great quantities of poisoned wine and plans to kill them all at a feast, keeping only the southerners here."

sentences.zh: 驍果皆懼，轉相告語，反謀益急。

translations.literal: The elite guard were all afraid; they told one another in turn, and the plot to rebel grew more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The guards were terrified. Rumor spread from man to man, and the conspiracy gathered speed.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，德戡悉召驍果軍吏，諭以所為，皆曰：「唯將軍命！」

translations.literal: On the day Yimao, Dekan summoned all the elite guard officers, explained what was to be done, and all said: "We obey the general's command alone!"
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yimao, Dekan summoned all the elite guard officers and laid out the plan. They answered as one, "We follow the general's command alone!"

sentences.zh: 是日，風霾晝昏。

translations.literal: That day, wind and dust made the daylight dim.
translations.idiomatic: That day a dusty wind darkened the daylight.

sentences.zh: 晡後，德戡盜御廄馬，潛厲兵刃。

translations.literal: After the hour of shen, Dekan stole horses from the imperial stables and secretly sharpened weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In the late afternoon Dekan stole horses from the imperial stables and quietly readied weapons.

sentences.zh: 是夕，元禮、裴虔通直閣下，專主殿內；

translations.literal: That evening Yuan Li and Pei Qiantong kept watch below the palace apartments and had sole charge within the halls;
translations.idiomatic: That evening Yuan Li and Pei Qiantong stood watch below the palace apartments and held sole authority within the halls;

sentences.zh: 唐奉義主閉城門，與虔通相知，諸門皆不下鍵。

translations.literal: Tang Fengyi was in charge of closing the city gates; he was in league with Qiantong, and none of the gates were barred.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Fengyi controlled the city gates. He was in league with Qiantong, and none of the gates were barred.

sentences.zh: 至三更，德戡於東城集兵得數萬人，舉火與城外相應。

translations.literal: At the third watch Dekan mustered troops in the eastern city until he had tens of thousands, raised fires, and signaled to those outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: At the third watch Dekan assembled tens of thousands of men in the eastern city, lit fires, and signaled to forces outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 帝望見火，且聞外喧囂，問何事。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw the fires and also heard the uproar outside; he asked what was happening.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor saw the fires and heard the clamor outside. He asked what was going on.

sentences.zh: 虔通對曰：「草坊失火，外人共救之耳。」

translations.literal: Qiantong replied: "The hay storehouse has caught fire; people outside are all helping to put it out."
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong answered, "The hay storehouse has caught fire. People outside are helping to put it out."

sentences.zh: 時內外隔絕，帝以為然。

translations.literal: At that time inside and outside were cut off from one another, and the Emperor believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside were cut off from each other, and the Emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 智及與孟秉於城外集千餘人，劫候衛虎賁馮普樂佈兵分守衢巷。

translations.literal: Zhiji and Meng Bing gathered more than a thousand men outside the city, seized the guard Tiger Guard Feng Pule, and deployed troops to hold the streets and lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the walls Zhiji and Meng Bing mustered more than a thousand men, seized guard Tiger Guard Feng Pule, and posted troops to hold the streets and lanes.

sentences.zh: 燕王倓覺有變，夜，穿芳林門側水竇而入，至玄武門，詭奏曰：「臣猝中風，命懸俄頃，請得面辭。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan, Yang Dan, sensed that something was amiss; at night he slipped through the water conduit beside Fanglin Gate, reached Xuanyuan Gate, and falsely reported: "Your subject has suddenly suffered a stroke; my life hangs by a moment—may I be granted a farewell audience."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan, Yang Dan, sensed trouble. That night he crept through the water conduit beside Fanglin Gate to Xuanyuan Gate and sent in a false report: "I have been stricken suddenly by paralysis; my life hangs by a thread—may I take leave of Your Majesty in person?"

sentences.zh: 裴虔通等不以聞，執囚之。

translations.literal: Pei Qiantong and the others did not pass the message on and seized and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Qiantong and his confederates did not relay the message and seized the prince.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，天未明，德戡授虔通兵，以代諸門衛士。

translations.literal: On the day Bingchen, before dawn, Dekan gave troops to Qiantong to replace the gate guards at every gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingchen, before dawn, Dekan handed troops to Qiantong to replace the guards at every gate.

sentences.zh: 虔通自門將數百騎至成象殿，宿衛者傳呼有賊；

translations.literal: Qiantong himself led several hundred horsemen from the gate to Chenxiang Hall; the night guards passed the cry that there were bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong himself led several hundred horsemen from the gate to Chenxiang Hall. The night guards shouted that bandits were at hand;

sentences.zh: 虔通乃還，閉諸門，獨開東門，驅殿內宿衛者令出，皆投仗而走。

translations.literal: Qiantong then returned, closed all the gates, opened only the eastern gate alone, drove the night guards within the hall to come out, and all cast down their weapons and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong turned back, shut every gate, opened only the east gate, drove the guards out of the hall, and they all threw down their weapons and fled.

sentences.zh: 右屯衛將軍獨孤盛謂虔通曰：「何物兵，形勢太異！」

translations.literal: Right Army Guard general Dugu Sheng said to Qiantong: "What sort of troops are these—the situation is far too strange!"
translations.idiomatic: Right Army Guard general Dugu Sheng said to Qiantong, "What sort of troops are these? The situation is all wrong!"

sentences.zh: 虔通曰：「事勢已然，不預將軍事；

translations.literal: Qiantong said: "The situation is already settled; this does not concern the general;
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong said, "The matter is already decided. It does not concern you, General;

sentences.zh: 將軍慎毋動！」

translations.literal: the general had best not stir!"
translations.idiomatic: you had best not move!"

sentences.zh: 盛大罵曰：「老賊，是何物語！」

translations.literal: Sheng cursed loudly: "Old traitor—what sort of talk is this!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng cursed, "You old traitor—what kind of talk is that!"

sentences.zh: 不及被甲，與左右十餘人拒戰，為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: He had no time to don armor; with a dozen or so followers he resisted and fought, and was killed by the mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: He had no time to arm himself. With a dozen followers he fought back and was killed by the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 盛，楷之弟也。

translations.literal: Sheng was the younger brother of Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was the younger brother of Dugu Kai.

sentences.zh: 千牛獨孤開遠帥殿內兵數百人詣玄武門，叩閣請曰：「兵仗尚全，猶堪破賊。

translations.literal: Thousand-Ox Dugu Kaiyuan led several hundred troops from within the hall to Xuanyuan Gate, knocked on the gate tower, and pleaded: "Our arms are still intact; we can still break the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-Ox Dugu Kaiyuan led several hundred men from within the palace to Xuanyuan Gate, knocked on the gate tower, and pleaded, "Our arms are still intact. We can still defeat the rebels.

sentences.zh: 陛下若出臨戰，人情自定；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty comes out in person to fight, men's hearts will settle of themselves;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty comes out to lead the fight, the men will steady themselves;

sentences.zh: 不然，禍今至矣！」

translations.literal: if not, disaster will arrive this very moment!"
translations.idiomatic: otherwise disaster will strike at once!"

sentences.zh: 竟無應者，軍士稍散。

translations.literal: In the end there was no response; the soldiers gradually dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: No answer came. The soldiers gradually drifted away.

sentences.zh: 賊執開遠，義而釋之。

translations.literal: The rebels seized Kaiyuan but, deeming him righteous, released him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized Kaiyuan but, judging him righteous, let him go.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝選驍健官奴數百人置玄武門，謂之給使，以備非常，待遇優厚，至以宮人賜之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had selected several hundred sturdy palace slaves and stationed them at Xuanyuan Gate, calling them attendants-on-call, to guard against emergencies; they were treated with exceptional favor, even to the point of being given palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Emperor had picked several hundred sturdy palace slaves for Xuanyuan Gate, calling them attendants-on-call, to meet emergencies. They were treated with exceptional favor, even given palace women as wives.

sentences.zh: 司宮魏氏為帝所信，化及等結之使為內應。

translations.literal: Palace stewardess Lady Wei was trusted by the Emperor; Huaji and the others won her over to serve as an inside contact.
translations.idiomatic: Palace stewardess Lady Wei enjoyed the Emperor's trust. Huaji and the others won her over as an inside contact.

sentences.zh: 是日，魏氏矯詔悉聽給使出外，倉猝之際，無一人在者。

translations.literal: That day Lady Wei forged an edict allowing all the attendants-on-call to go outside; in the sudden crisis not a single one remained.
translations.idiomatic: That day Lady Wei forged an edict sending every attendant-on-call outside. In the sudden crisis, not one was left at the gate.

sentences.zh: 德戡等引兵自玄武門入，帝聞亂，易服逃西閣。

translations.literal: Dekan and the others led troops in through Xuanyuan Gate; the Emperor heard of the disturbance, changed clothes, and fled to the western pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan and his men entered through Xuanyuan Gate. Hearing the uproar, the Emperor changed clothes and fled to the western pavilion.

sentences.zh: 虔通與元禮進兵排左閣，魏氏啟之，遂入永巷，問：「陛下安在？」

translations.literal: Qiantong and Yuan Li advanced troops to force the left gate; Lady Wei opened it, and they entered the Long Lane, asking: "Where is Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong and Yuan Li forced the left gate. Lady Wei opened it, and they entered the Long Lane calling, "Where is Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 有美人出，指之。

translations.literal: A palace beauty came out and pointed the way.
translations.idiomatic: A palace woman came out and pointed the way.

sentences.zh: 校尉令狐行達拔刀直進，帝映窗扉謂行達曰：「汝欲殺我邪？」

translations.literal: Commandant Linghu Xingda drew his sword and advanced straight in; the Emperor, visible through the window frame, said to Xingda: "Do you wish to kill me?"
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Linghu Xingda drew his sword and rushed in. The Emperor, seen through the window, said to him, "Do you mean to kill me?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣不敢，但欲奉陛下西還耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject dares not; I only wish to escort Your Majesty back west."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I would not dare. I only wish to escort Your Majesty back west."

sentences.zh: 因扶帝下閣。

translations.literal: He thereupon helped the Emperor down from the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He helped the Emperor down from the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 虔通，本帝為晉王時親信左右也，帝見之，謂曰：「卿非我敵人乎！

translations.literal: Qiantong had been a trusted attendant when the Emperor was Prince of Jin; seeing him, the Emperor said: "Are you not my enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong had been a trusted attendant when the Emperor was still Prince of Jin. Seeing him, the Emperor said, "So you are my enemy after all!

sentences.zh: 何恨而反？」

translations.literal: What grudge makes you rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: What grievance drives you to rebel?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣不敢反，但將士思歸，欲奉陛下還京師耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject dares not rebel; it is only that the officers and soldiers long to return home and wish to escort Your Majesty back to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I would not rebel. The men only long to go home and wish to escort Your Majesty back to the capital."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕方欲歸，正為上江米船未至，今與汝歸耳！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I was just about to return; I was only waiting for the rice boats from upriver. Now I shall return with you!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I was about to return anyway—I was only waiting for the rice boats from upriver. Very well, let us go back together!"

sentences.zh: 虔通因勒兵守之。

translations.literal: Qiantong thereupon drew up troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong then posted troops to guard him.

sentences.zh: 至旦，孟秉以甲騎迎化及，化及戰慄不能言，人有來謁之者，但俯首據鞍稱罪過。

translations.literal: At dawn Meng Bing met Huaji with armored cavalry; Huaji trembled and could not speak; when anyone came to pay respects he only bowed his head over the saddle and confessed his faults.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Meng Bing met Huaji with armored cavalry. Huaji shook so badly he could not speak. When anyone came to pay respects he only bowed over his saddle and confessed his crimes.

sentences.zh: 化及至城門，德戡迎謁，引入朝堂，號為丞相。

translations.literal: When Huaji reached the city gate, Dekan met and paid homage to him, led him into the court hall, and hailed him as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji reached the gate, Dekan received him and led him into the court hall, proclaiming him chief minister.

sentences.zh: 裴虔通謂帝曰：「百官悉在朝堂，陛下須親出慰勞。」

translations.literal: Pei Qiantong said to the Emperor: "All the officials are in the court hall; Your Majesty must go out in person to comfort and encourage them."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Qiantong told the Emperor, "All the officials are in the court hall. Your Majesty must go out in person to reassure them."

sentences.zh: 進其從騎，逼帝乘之；

translations.literal: He brought forward the Emperor's escort horses and forced the Emperor to mount;
translations.idiomatic: He brought up the Emperor's escort horses and forced him to mount;

sentences.zh: 帝嫌其鞍勒弊，更易新者，乃乘之。

translations.literal: the Emperor disliked the worn saddle and bridle and had them replaced with new ones before he would ride.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor disliked the worn saddle and bridle and had new ones brought before he would ride.

sentences.zh: 虔通執轡挾刀出宮門，賊徒喜噪動地。

translations.literal: Qiantong held the reins and a knife at his side as they left the palace gate; the rebels shouted for joy until the ground shook.
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong held the reins with a knife at his side as they left the palace. The rebels roared with joy until the earth seemed to shake.

sentences.zh: 化及揚言曰：「何用持此物出，亟還與手。」

translations.literal: Huaji proclaimed aloud: "What use is it to bring this thing out? Quickly bring it back and deal with it by your own hands."
translations.idiomatic: Huaji shouted, "Why bring this thing out at all? Take it back at once and finish it yourselves."

sentences.zh: 帝問：「世基何在？」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked: "Where is Shiji?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked, "Where is Shiji?"

sentences.zh: 賊黨馬文舉曰：「已梟首矣！」

translations.literal: The rebel Ma Wenchu said: "His head is already on display!"
translations.idiomatic: Rebel Ma Wenchu said, "His head is already on display!"

sentences.zh: 於是引帝還至寢殿，虔通、德戡等拔白刃侍立。

translations.literal: They then led the Emperor back to the sleeping hall; Qiantong, Dekan, and the others drew bare blades and stood guard.
translations.idiomatic: They led the Emperor back to the sleeping hall. Qiantong, Dekan, and the others drew naked blades and stood guard.

sentences.zh: 帝歎曰：「我何罪至此？」

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed: "What crime have I committed to come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sighed, "What crime have I committed to come to this?"

sentences.zh: 文舉曰：「陛下違棄宗廟，巡遊不息，外勤征討，內極奢淫，使丁壯盡於矢刃，女弱填於溝壑，四民喪業，盜賊蜂起；

translations.literal: Wenchu said: "Your Majesty abandoned the ancestral temples and toured without cease; abroad you waged campaigns incessantly, within you indulged to the utmost in luxury and lust, until able-bodied men were exhausted by sword and arrow and women and children filled the ditches and gullies; the four classes lost their livelihoods and bandits rose like bees;
translations.idiomatic: Wenchu said, "Your Majesty abandoned the ancestral temples and never stopped touring. Abroad you waged endless campaigns; at home you indulged in luxury and lust until every able-bodied man fell to sword and arrow and women and children filled the ditches. The people lost their livelihoods and bandits swarmed like bees;

sentences.zh: 專任佞諛，飾非拒諫；

translations.literal: you entrusted power solely to flatterers, covered up faults and rejected remonstrance;
translations.idiomatic: you trusted only flatterers, covered your faults, and rejected honest counsel;

sentences.zh: 何謂無罪！」

translations.literal: how can you say you are without crime!"
translations.idiomatic: how can you say you are without crime!"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我實負百姓；

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I have indeed failed the people;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I have indeed failed the people;

sentences.zh: 至於爾輩，榮祿兼極，何乃如是！

translations.literal: as for you people, honor and salary have reached their height—why act thus!
translations.idiomatic: but as for you, honor and salary have reached their height—why treat me thus!

sentences.zh: 今日之事，孰為首邪？」

translations.literal: In today's affair, who is the ringleader?"
translations.idiomatic: Of today's affair, who is the ringleader?"

sentences.zh: 德戡曰：「溥天同怨，何止一人！」

translations.literal: Dekan said: "All under Heaven share the same grievance—how could it be only one man!"
translations.idiomatic: Dekan said, "All under Heaven shares the same grievance—how could it be only one man!"

sentences.zh: 化及又使封德彝數帝罪，帝曰：「卿乃士人，何為亦爾！」

translations.literal: Huaji also had Feng Deyi enumerate the Emperor's crimes; the Emperor said: "You are a scholar—why act thus as well!"
translations.idiomatic: Huaji also had Feng Deyi list the Emperor's crimes. The Emperor said, "You are a scholar—why do you join in this!"

sentences.zh: 德彝赧然而退。

translations.literal: Deyi flushed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi flushed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝愛子趙王杲，年十二，在帝側，號慟不已，虔通斬之，血濺御服。

translations.literal: The Emperor's beloved son, the Prince of Zhao Yang Gao, twelve years old, was at the Emperor's side wailing without cease; Qiantong beheaded him, and blood splashed the imperial robes.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's beloved son, twelve-year-old Prince of Zhao Yang Gao, stood at his side wailing without cease. Qiantong beheaded him, and blood splashed the imperial robes.

sentences.zh: 賊欲弒帝，帝曰：「天子死自有法，何得加以鋒刃！

translations.literal: The rebels wished to assassinate the Emperor; the Emperor said: "When a Son of Heaven dies there is a proper method—how can you apply the blade!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels meant to kill the Emperor. He said, "A Son of Heaven has a proper way to die—why use the blade!

sentences.zh: 取鴆酒來！」

translations.literal: Bring poisoned wine!"
translations.idiomatic: Bring poisoned wine!"

sentences.zh: 文舉等不許，使令狐行達頓帝令坐。

translations.literal: Wenchu and the others would not allow it and had Linghu Xingda seize the Emperor and force him to sit.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchu and the others refused and had Linghu Xingda seize the Emperor and force him to sit.

sentences.zh: 帝自解練巾授行達，縊殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself untied his white silk scarf and gave it to Xingda, who strangled him with it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor untied his own white silk scarf and gave it to Xingda, who strangled him with it.

sentences.zh: 初，帝自知必及於難，常以罌貯毒藥自隨，謂所幸諸姬曰：「若賊至，汝曹當先飲之，然後我飲。」

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor, knowing he would surely meet disaster, had always carried poison in a jar at his side and told his favored consorts: "If bandits come, you must drink first, and then I shall drink."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, knowing disaster was inevitable, the Emperor had always kept poison in a jar at hand and told his favored consorts, "If rebels come, you must drink first, and then I will drink."

sentences.zh: 及亂，顧索藥，左右皆逃散，竟不能得。

translations.literal: When the disturbance came he looked about for the poison, but those at his side had all fled and scattered, and in the end he could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: When the disturbance came he looked for the poison, but his attendants had all fled and he could not obtain it.

sentences.zh: 蕭后與宮人撤漆床板為小棺，與趙王杲同殯於西院流珠堂。

translations.literal: Empress Xiao and the palace women took lacquered bed boards to make a small coffin and buried the Prince of Zhao Gao with the Emperor in Liuzhu Hall in the western courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiao and the palace women stripped lacquered bed boards to make a small coffin and buried Prince Zhao Gao with the Emperor in Liuzhu Hall in the western courtyard.

sentences.zh: 帝每巡幸，常以蜀王秀自隨，囚於驍果營。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor went on tour he usually had the Prince of Shu Yang Xiu accompany him and kept him imprisoned in the elite guard camp.
translations.idiomatic: On his tours the Emperor usually kept Prince of Shu Yang Xiu with him, imprisoned in the elite guard camp.

sentences.zh: 化及弒帝，欲奉秀立之，眾議不可，乃殺秀及其七男。

translations.literal: After Huaji murdered the Emperor he wished to install Xiu as sovereign; the assembly would not agree, so he killed Xiu and his seven sons.
translations.idiomatic: After murdering the Emperor, Huaji wished to set up Xiu as sovereign. The assembly refused, so he killed Xiu and his seven sons.

sentences.zh: 又殺齊王暕及其二子並燕王倓，隋氏宗室、外戚，無少長皆死。

translations.literal: He also killed the Prince of Qi Yang Jian and his two sons, and the Prince of Yan Yang Dan; of the Sui imperial clan and affinal kin, none young or old was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed Prince of Qi Yang Jian and his two sons, and Prince of Yan Yang Dan. Of the Sui imperial clan and affinal kin, none young or old was spared.

sentences.zh: 唯秦王浩素與智及往來，且以計全之。

translations.literal: Only the Prince of Qin Yang Hao, who had long been on familiar terms with Zhiji and was spared by his stratagem, survived.
translations.idiomatic: Only Prince of Qin Yang Hao survived, having long been friendly with Zhiji and been spared through his connivance.

sentences.zh: 齊王暕素失愛於帝，恆相猜忌。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi Jian had long lost the Emperor's favor, and they were constantly suspicious of each other.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Jian had long lost the Emperor's favor, and father and son were constantly suspicious of each other.

sentences.zh: 帝聞亂，顧蕭后曰：「得非阿孩邪？」

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of the disturbance he turned to Empress Xiao and said: "Could it be Ahai?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard of the disturbance he turned to Empress Xiao and said, "Could it be Ahai?"

sentences.zh: 化及使人就第誅暕，暕謂帝使收之，曰：「詔使且緩兒，兒不負國家！」

translations.literal: Huaji sent men to Jian's residence to execute him; Jian thought it was an imperial envoy come to arrest him and said: "Imperial envoy, spare your son a little—your son has not failed the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Huaji sent men to Jian's residence to kill him. Jian thought they were imperial envoys come to arrest him and said, "Imperial envoy, spare your son a moment—your son has not failed the state!"

sentences.zh: 賊曳至街中，斬之，暕竟不知殺者為誰，父子至死不相明。

translations.literal: The rebels dragged him into the street and beheaded him; Jian to the end did not know who his killers were, and father and son never understood each other even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dragged him into the street and beheaded him. Jian never knew who his killers were, and father and son died without ever understanding each other.

sentences.zh: 又殺內史待郎虞世基、御史大夫裴蘊、左翊衛大將軍來護兒、秘書監袁充、右翊衛將軍宇文協、千牛宇文皛、梁公蕭鉅等及其子。

translations.literal: He also killed Palace Secretariat vice director Yu Shiji, Censor-in-chief Pei Yun, Left Army Guard general Lai Huer, Secretariat director Yuan Chong, Right Army Guard general Yuwen Xie, Thousand-Ox Yuwen Jiao, Duke of Liang Xiao Ju, and their sons.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed Palace Secretariat vice director Yu Shiji, Censor-in-chief Pei Yun, Left Army Guard general Lai Huer, Secretariat director Yuan Chong, Right Army Guard general Yuwen Xie, Thousand-Ox Yuwen Jiao, Duke of Liang Xiao Ju, and their sons.

sentences.zh: 鉅，琮之弟子也。

translations.literal: Ju was the nephew of Xiao Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was the nephew of Xiao Cong.

sentences.zh: 難將作，江陽長張惠紹馳告裴蘊，與惠紹謀矯詔發郭下兵收化及等，扣門援帝。

translations.literal: Just before the crisis Jiangyang magistrate Zhang Huishao galloped to inform Pei Yun; with Huishao he plotted to forge an edict mobilizing troops outside the city walls to seize Huaji and the others and batter the gates to rescue the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Just before the crisis, Jiangyang magistrate Zhang Huishao galloped to warn Pei Yun. Together they plotted to forge an edict, mobilize troops outside the walls to seize Huaji and his confederates, and batter the gates to rescue the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 議定，遣報虞世基；

translations.literal: When the plan was settled they sent word to Yu Shiji;
translations.idiomatic: When the plan was settled they sent word to Yu Shiji;

sentences.zh: 世基疑告反者不實，抑而不許。

translations.literal: Shiji doubted that the report of rebellion was genuine and suppressed it without approval.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji doubted the report of rebellion was genuine and refused to act.

sentences.zh: 須臾，難作，蘊歎曰：「謀及播郎，竟誤人事！」

translations.literal: In a moment the crisis broke out; Yun sighed: "We consulted the Broad Lord and in the end ruined the affair!"
translations.idiomatic: A moment later the crisis broke out. Yun sighed, "We consulted the Broad Lord and ruined everything!"

sentences.zh: 虞世基宗人人及謂世基子符璽郎熙曰：「事勢已然，吾將濟卿南渡，同死何益？」

translations.literal: Yu Shiji's clansman Ren Renji said to Shiji's son, seal keeper Xi: "The situation is already settled; I will help you cross south—what use is dying together?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiji's clansman Ren Renji said to Shiji's son, seal keeper Xi, "The situation is settled. I will help you escape south—what use is dying together?"

sentences.zh: 熙曰：「棄父背君，求生何地？

translations.literal: Xi said: "Abandoning my father and betraying my sovereign—where could I seek life?
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "Abandon my father and betray my sovereign—where could I go to live?

sentences.zh: 感尊之懷，自此決矣！」

translations.literal: Touched by your honorable feeling, I am resolved from this moment!"
translations.idiomatic: Your honorable feeling moves me—I am resolved from this moment!"

sentences.zh: 世基弟世南抱世基號泣，請以身代，化及不許。

translations.literal: Shiji's younger brother Shinan embraced Shiji and wailed, begging to die in his place; Huaji would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji's younger brother Shinan embraced him and wailed, begging to die in his place. Huaji refused.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎裴矩知必將有亂，雖廝役皆厚遇之，又建策為驍果娶婦；

translations.literal: Yellow Gate vice director Pei Ju, knowing disorder was sure to come, treated even menials with great favor and also proposed that wives be found for the elite guard;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate vice director Pei Ju, foreseeing disorder, treated even servants generously and proposed finding wives for the elite guard;

sentences.zh: 及亂作，賊皆曰：「非裴黃門之罪。」

translations.literal: when the disturbance broke out the rebels all said: "This is not Vice Director Pei's fault."
translations.idiomatic: when the disturbance broke out the rebels all said, "This is not Vice Director Pei's fault."

sentences.zh: 既而化及至，矩迎拜馬首，故得免。

translations.literal: When Huaji arrived, Ju met and bowed at his horse's head and therefore was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji arrived, Ju bowed at his horse's head and was spared.

sentences.zh: 化及以蘇威不預朝政，亦免之。

translations.literal: Huaji also spared Su Wei because he had not taken part in court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji also spared Su Wei because he had not taken part in governing.

sentences.zh: 威名位素重，往參化及；

translations.literal: Wei's name and position had long been weighty; he went to pay respects to Huaji;
translations.idiomatic: Wei's name and standing were weighty; he went to pay respects to Huaji;

sentences.zh: 化及集眾而見之，曲加殊禮。

translations.literal: Huaji assembled the crowd to receive him and showed him exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji assembled the crowd to receive him and treated him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 百官悉詣朝堂賀，給事郎許善心獨不至。

translations.literal: All the officials went to the court hall to offer congratulations; only Secretariat attendant Xu Shansin did not come.
translations.idiomatic: All the officials went to the court hall to congratulate; only Secretariat attendant Xu Shansin stayed away.

sentences.zh: 許弘仁馳告之曰：「天子已崩，宇文將軍攝政，闔朝文武咸集。

translations.literal: Xu Hongren galloped to tell him: "The Son of Heaven is already dead; General Yuwen holds the regency; the whole court is assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hongren galloped to tell him, "The Son of Heaven is dead. General Yuwen holds the regency. The whole court is assembled.

sentences.zh: 天道人事自有代終，何預於叔而低回若此？」

translations.literal: Heaven's way and human affairs have their own cycles of ending—what concern is it of yours, uncle, to hesitate thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth have their cycles—why should you, uncle, hang back like this?"

sentences.zh: 善心怒，不肯行。

translations.literal: Shansin was angry and refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: Shansin was angry and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 弘仁反走上馬，泣而去。

translations.literal: Hongren turned, mounted his horse, wept, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Hongren turned, mounted his horse in tears, and rode away.

sentences.zh: 化及遣人就家擒至朝堂，既而釋之。

translations.literal: Huaji sent men to seize him at his home and bring him to the court hall, then released him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji sent men to seize him at home and bring him to court, then released him.

sentences.zh: 善心不舞蹈而出，化及怒曰：「此人大負氣！」

translations.literal: Shansin left without performing the congratulatory dance; Huaji said angrily: "This man is full of pride!"
translations.idiomatic: Shansin left without performing the congratulatory dance. Huaji said angrily, "This man is full of pride!"

sentences.zh: 覆命擒還，殺之。

translations.literal: He ordered him seized again and killed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him seized again and killed.

sentences.zh: 其母範氏，年九十二，撫柩不哭，曰：「能死國難，吾有子矣！」

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Fan, ninety-two years old, stroked the coffin without weeping and said: "To die for the state's calamity— I have a son!"
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Fan, ninety-two years old, stroked the coffin without weeping and said, "To die for the state's calamity—I have a true son!"

sentences.zh: 因臥不食，十餘日而卒。

translations.literal: She thereupon took to her bed and would not eat, and died after more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: She took to her bed and refused food, dying after more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 唐王之入關也，張季珣之弟仲琰為上洛令，帥吏民拒守，部下殺之以降。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Tang entered the passes, Zhang Jixun's younger brother Zhongyan was magistrate of Shangluo; he led officials and people to resist and hold out, but his subordinates killed him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Tang entered the passes, Zhang Jixun's younger brother Zhongyan was magistrate of Shangluo. He led officials and people in resistance until his subordinates killed him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之亂，仲琰弟琮為千牛左右，化及殺之，兄弟三人皆死國難，時人愧之。

translations.literal: In Yuwen Huaji's disturbance Zhongyan's younger brother Cong was a Thousand-Ox attendant; Huaji killed him. All three brothers died for the state's calamity, and men of the time were shamed by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuwen Huaji's coup Zhongyan's younger brother Cong was a Thousand-Ox attendant; Huaji killed him. All three brothers died for the state, and contemporaries were shamed by comparison.

sentences.zh: 化及自稱大丞相，總百揆。

translations.literal: Huaji styled himself grand chief minister and oversaw all government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji styled himself grand chief minister and took charge of all government affairs.

sentences.zh: 以皇后令立秦王浩為帝，居別宮，令發詔畫敕書而已，仍以兵監守之。

translations.literal: By the empress's order he installed the Prince of Qin Hao as emperor, housed him in a separate palace, allowed him only to issue edicts and sign rescripts, and still kept troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: By the empress's order he installed Prince of Qin Hao as emperor in a separate palace, allowed him only to issue edicts and sign rescripts, and kept troops to guard him.

sentences.zh: 化及以弟智及為左僕射，士及為內史令，裴矩為右僕射。

translations.literal: Huaji appointed his younger brother Zhiji left vice director, Shiqi inner secretariat director, and Pei Ju right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji appointed his younger brother Zhiji left vice director, Shiqi inner secretariat director, and Pei Ju right vice director.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，徙秦公世民為趙公。

translations.literal: On the day Yimao, the Duke of Qin Shimin was transferred to be Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yimao, Duke of Qin Li Shimin was made Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，隋恭帝詔以十郡益唐國，仍以唐王為相國，總百揆，唐國置丞相以下官，又加九錫。

translations.literal: On the day Wuchen, Emperor Gong of Sui issued an edict adding ten commanderies to the state of Tang, again making the Prince of Tang chief minister overseeing all government affairs, establishing chief minister and subordinate offices for the state of Tang, and also bestowing the nine gifts of honor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuchen, Emperor Gong of Sui decreed ten more commanderies for the state of Tang, again named the Prince of Tang chief minister over all government affairs, established a chief minister's office for Tang, and added the nine gifts of honor.

sentences.zh: 王謂僚屬曰：「此諂諛者所為耳。

translations.literal: The Prince said to his staff: "This is the work of flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince told his staff, "This is the work of flatterers.

sentences.zh: 孤秉大政而自加寵錫，可乎？

translations.literal: I hold great power and bestow honors on myself—can that be right?
translations.idiomatic: I hold supreme power and bestow honors on myself—can that be right?

sentences.zh: 必若循魏、晉之跡，彼皆繁文偽飾，欺天罔人；

translations.literal: If one must follow the tracks of Wei and Jin, those were all ornate forms and false display, deceiving Heaven and deluding men;
translations.idiomatic: If we must follow Wei and Jin, those were ornate frauds that deceived Heaven and deluded men;

sentences.zh: 考其實不及五霸，而求名欲過三王，此孤常所非笑，竊亦恥之。」

translations.literal: examined in reality they did not equal the Five Hegemons, yet in seeking fame they wished to surpass the Three Kings—this I have always mocked and privately am ashamed of."
translations.idiomatic: in reality they did not equal the Five Hegemons, yet they sought fame beyond the Three Kings—I have always mocked that and am ashamed of it."

sentences.zh: 或曰：「歷代所行，亦何可廢！」

translations.literal: Someone said: "What every dynasty has practiced—how can it be abolished!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "What every dynasty has practiced—how can we abolish it!"

sentences.zh: 王曰：「堯、舜、湯、武，各因其時，取與異道，皆推其至誠以應天順人，未聞夏、商之末必效唐、虞之禪也。

translations.literal: The Prince said: "Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu each acted according to their times, taking and giving by different paths, all extending their utmost sincerity to respond to Heaven and accord with men—I have never heard that the ends of Xia and Shang must imitate the abdications of Tang and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince said, "Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu each acted according to their times by different paths, all extending utmost sincerity to respond to Heaven and accord with the people. I have never heard that the ends of Xia and Shang must imitate the abdications of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 若使少帝有知，必不肯為；

translations.literal: If the young emperor had understanding, he would surely refuse;
translations.idiomatic: If the young emperor had understanding, he would surely refuse;

sentences.zh: 若其無知，孤自尊而飾讓，平生素心所不為也。」

translations.literal: if he had no understanding, for me to exalt myself while feigning modest refusal is what my heart has never done in ordinary times."
translations.idiomatic: if he has none, for me to exalt myself while feigning modest refusal is what my heart has never condoned."

sentences.zh: 但改丞相為相國府，其九錫殊禮，皆歸之有司。

translations.literal: He only changed chief minister to chief minister's office; the special rites of the nine gifts of honor were all returned to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: He only changed the title to chief minister's office and returned the special rites of the nine gifts to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及以左武衛將軍陳稜為江都太守，綜領留事。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji appointed Left Martial Guard general Chen Ling Jiangdu prefect to oversee affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Huaji appointed Left Martial Guard general Chen Ling Jiangdu prefect to oversee affairs left behind.

sentences.zh: 壬申，令內外戒嚴，雲欲還長安。

translations.literal: On the day Renshen he ordered alert within and without, saying he wished to return to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renshen he ordered alert within and without, announcing a return to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 皇后六宮皆依舊式為御宮，營前別立帳，化及視事其中，仗衛部伍，皆擬乘輿。

translations.literal: The empress and the six palaces were arranged in the imperial palace according to the old forms; a separate tent was set up before the camp where Huaji conducted business; guards and formations all imitated the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The empress and the six palaces were arranged in the imperial style. A separate tent was set before the camp where Huaji conducted business; guards and formations all imitated the imperial establishment.

sentences.zh: 奪江都人舟楫，取彭城水路西歸。

translations.literal: He seized boats from the people of Jiangdu and took the Pengcheng water route westward homeward.
translations.idiomatic: He seized boats from the people of Jiangdu and took the Pengcheng water route westward.

sentences.zh: 以折衝郎將沈光驍勇，使將給使營於禁內。

translations.literal: Because Strike Force commandant Shen Guang was valiant and fierce, he had him lead the attendants-on-call encamped within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Because Strike Force commandant Shen Guang was valiant, he had him lead the attendants-on-call encamped within the forbidden precinct.

sentences.zh: 行至顯福宮，虎賁郎將麥孟才、虎牙郎錢傑與光謀曰：「吾儕受先帝厚恩，今俯首事仇，受其驅帥，何面目視息世間哉！

translations.literal: When they reached Xianfu Palace, Tiger Guard commandant Mai Mengcai, Tiger Tusk commandant Qian Jie, and Guang plotted together, saying: "We received thick favor from the former emperor; now we bow our heads and serve the enemy, driven and commanded by them—what face have we to draw breath in this world!
translations.idiomatic: At Xianfu Palace, Tiger Guard commandant Mai Mengcai, Tiger Tusk commandant Qian Jie, and Guang plotted together. "We received great favor from the former emperor," they said. "Now we bow to the enemy and take their orders—what face have we to live on in this world!

sentences.zh: 吾必欲殺之，死無所恨！」

translations.literal: We must kill him—death will hold no regret!"
translations.idiomatic: We must kill him—death will hold no regret!"

sentences.zh: 光泣曰：「是所望於將軍也！」

translations.literal: Guang wept and said: "That is what I have hoped for from you generals!"
translations.idiomatic: Guang wept and said, "That is exactly what I have hoped for from you!"

sentences.zh: 孟才乃糾合恩舊，帥所將數千人，期以晨起將發時襲化及。

translations.literal: Mengcai thereupon gathered old comrades and led the several thousand men under his command, fixing the time for dawn when the army was about to set out to attack Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcai gathered old comrades and led several thousand men, fixing dawn when the army was about to march as the moment to strike Huaji.

sentences.zh: 語洩，化及夜與腹心走出營外，留人告司馬德戡等，使討之。

translations.literal: The plan leaked; Huaji fled the camp at night with his intimates, left men to inform Sima Dekan and the others, and had them suppress the plot.
translations.idiomatic: The plan leaked. Huaji fled the camp at night with his intimates, sent word to Sima Dekan and the others, and had them suppress the plot.

sentences.zh: 光聞營內喧，知事覺，即襲化及營，空無所獲，值內史侍郎元敏，數而斬之。

translations.literal: Guang heard commotion within the camp, knew the plot had been discovered, and immediately attacked Huaji's camp; finding nothing there, he encountered Vice Director of the Secretariat Yuan Min, rebuked him, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing uproar in the camp, Guang realized the plot had leaked and at once struck at Huaji's camp. He found nothing there, but came upon Vice Director of the Secretariat Yuan Min, whom he rebuked and executed.

sentences.zh: 德戡引兵入圍之，殺光，其麾下數百人皆斗死，一無降者，孟才亦死。

translations.literal: Dekan led troops in to surround them, killed Guang; his several hundred followers all fought to the death, not one surrendered, and Mengcai also died.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan marched in and surrounded them, killing Guang. Several hundred of his men fought to the last man without a single surrender, and Mengcai died as well.

sentences.zh: 孟才，鐵杖之子也。

translations.literal: Mengcai was the son of Tiezhang.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcai was Tiezhang's son.

sentences.zh: 武康沈法興，世為郡著姓，宗族數千家。

translations.literal: Shen Faxing of Wukang was for generations a prominent clan of the commandery, his clan numbering several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Faxing of Wukang came from a locally prominent family whose clan numbered several thousand households over the generations.

sentences.zh: 法興為吳興太守，聞宇文化及弒逆，舉兵，以討化及為名。

translations.literal: Faxing was Administrator of Wuxing; hearing that Yuwen Huaji had committed regicide, he raised troops under the banner of punishing Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: As Administrator of Wuxing, Faxing raised troops when he learned of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, naming his campaign the punitive expedition against Huaji.

sentences.zh: 比至烏程，得精卒六萬，遂攻餘杭、毘陵、丹楊，皆下之，據江表十郡。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Wucheng he had gathered sixty thousand elite soldiers, then attacked Yuhang, Piling, and Danyang, took them all, and held ten commanderies south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Wucheng he had sixty thousand picked troops. He then captured Yuhang, Piling, and Danyang in succession and controlled ten commanderies south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 自稱江南道大總管，承製置百官。

translations.literal: He styled himself Grand Commander of the Jiangnan Circuit and, by imperial commission, established the full roster of officials.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed himself Grand Commander of the Jiangnan Circuit and appointed a full bureaucracy as though by imperial mandate.

sentences.zh: 東國公竇抗，唐王之妃兄也。

translations.literal: Eastern State Duke Dou Kang was the elder brother of the Prince of Tang's consort.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern State Duke Dou Kang was the elder brother of the Prince of Tang's wife.

sentences.zh: 煬帝使行長城於靈武；

translations.literal: Emperor Yang had sent him to oversee the Great Wall works at Lingwu;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang had posted him to oversee Great Wall construction at Lingwu;

sentences.zh: 聞唐王定關中，癸酉，帥靈武、鹽川等數郡來降。

translations.literal: On learning that the Prince of Tang had secured Guanzhong, on the day Guiyou he led several commanderies including Lingwu and Yanchuan to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that the Prince of Tang had consolidated Guanzhong, he submitted on the day Guiyou at the head of Lingwu, Yanchuan, and several other commanderies.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，稽胡寇富平，將軍王師仁擊破之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Ji barbarians raided Fuping; General Wang Shiren defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Ji raiders struck Fuping, but General Wang Shiren routed them.

sentences.zh: 又五萬餘人寇宜春，相國府咨議參軍竇軌將兵討之，戰於黃欽山。

translations.literal: More than fifty thousand others raided Yichun; Advisory Staff Officer Dou Gui of the Chancellor's Office led troops to suppress them and fought at Mount Huangqin.
translations.idiomatic: Another fifty thousand raided Yichun. Dou Gui, Advisory Staff Officer in the Chancellor's office, marched against them and gave battle at Mount Huangqin.

sentences.zh: 稽胡乘高縱火，官軍小卻；

translations.literal: The Ji barbarians took the heights and set fires; the government army fell back slightly;
translations.idiomatic: The Ji took the high ground and lit fires, and the government forces gave ground.

sentences.zh: 軌斬其部將十四人，拔隊中小校代之，勒兵復戰。

translations.literal: Gui beheaded fourteen of their subordinate officers, promoted squad leaders from the ranks to replace them, rallied the army, and fought again.
translations.idiomatic: Gui executed fourteen subordinate officers, promoted squad leaders from the ranks to fill their posts, reformed the line, and attacked again.

sentences.zh: 軌自將數百騎居軍後，令之曰：「聞鼓聲有不進者，自後斬之！」

translations.literal: Gui personally led several hundred horsemen at the rear of the army and ordered them, saying: "At the sound of the drum, any who do not advance—I shall cut them down from the rear!"
translations.idiomatic: Gui took personal command of several hundred cavalry at the rear and declared: "When the drum sounds, anyone who fails to advance—I will cut him down from behind!"

sentences.zh: 既而鼓之，將士爭先赴敵，稽胡射之不能止；

translations.literal: Then he sounded the drum; officers and soldiers vied to rush the enemy, and the Ji barbarians' arrows could not stop them;
translations.idiomatic: He beat the drum. Officers and men charged ahead of one another, and Ji archery could not halt them;

sentences.zh: 遂大破之，虜男女二萬口。

translations.literal: Thereupon he inflicted a great defeat and captured twenty thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: He routed them completely and took twenty thousand captives, men and women.

sentences.zh: 世子建成等至東都，軍於芒華苑；

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Li Jiancheng and the others reached the Eastern Capital and encamped at Manghua Park;
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Li Jiancheng and his forces reached the Eastern Capital and encamped at Manghua Park;

sentences.zh: 東都閉門不出，遣人招諭，不應。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital shut its gates and would not come out; they sent men to summon and instruct them, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital kept its gates closed. Envoys were sent to summon the city to terms, but there was no answer.

sentences.zh: 李密出軍爭之，小戰，各引去。

translations.literal: Li Mi sent out troops to contest them; after a small engagement, each side withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi marched out to oppose them. After a brief skirmish both sides withdrew.

sentences.zh: 城中多欲為內應者，趙公世民曰：「吾新定關中，根本未固，懸軍遠來，雖得東都，不能守也。」

translations.literal: Many in the city wished to act as inside collaborators; Duke of Zhao Li Shimin said: "We have just secured Guanzhong and our base is not yet firm; with an army far from home, even if we took the Eastern Capital we could not hold it."
translations.idiomatic: Many in the city were ready to open the gates from within, but Duke of Zhao Li Shimin said: "We have only just taken Guanzhong and our base is still unsettled. An army this far from home could not hold the Eastern Capital even if we took it."

sentences.zh: 遂不受。

translations.literal: Thereupon they did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore declined the offer.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，引軍還。

translations.literal: On the day Wuyin they led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuyin they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 世民曰：「城中見吾退，必來追躡。」

translations.literal: Li Shimin said: "When the city sees us retreat, they will surely come in pursuit."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin said: "Once they see us pull back, they are sure to pursue."

sentences.zh: 乃設三伏於三王陵以待之；

translations.literal: He thereupon set three ambushes at the Three Kings' Tombs to await them;
translations.idiomatic: He laid three ambushes at the Three Kings' Tombs.

sentences.zh: 段達果將萬餘人追之，遇伏而敗。

translations.literal: Duan Da indeed led more than ten thousand men in pursuit, encountered the ambushes, and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da duly pursued with more than ten thousand men, walked into the ambush, and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 世民逐北，抵其城下，斬四千餘級。

translations.literal: Li Shimin pursued the fleeing enemy to the foot of their city walls and beheaded more than four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin chased the routed army to the city walls and took more than four thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 遂置新安、宜陽二郡，使行軍總管史萬寶、盛彥師將兵鎮宜陽，呂紹宗、任瑰將兵鎮新安而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established the two commanderies Xin'an and Yiyang, had Mobile-Campaign Grand Commandants Shi Wanbao and Sheng Yanshi garrison Yiyang with troops, Lü Shaozong and Ren Gui garrison Xin'an with troops, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then set up the commanderies of Xin'an and Yiyang, left Shi Wanbao and Sheng Yanshi to hold Yiyang and Lü Shaozong and Ren Gui to hold Xin'an, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 初，五原通守櫟陽張長遜以中原大亂，舉郡附突厥，突厥以為割利特勒。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chief Secretary of Wuyuan Zhang Changsun of Liyang, because the Central Plains were in great disorder, submitted his entire commandery to the Turks, and the Turks made him Jiali Tegin.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Zhang Changsun of Liyang, chief secretary of Wuyuan, had submitted his whole commandery to the Turks amid the chaos in the Central Plains; the Turks enfeoffed him as Jiali Tegin.

sentences.zh: 郝瑗說薛舉，與梁師都及突厥連兵以取長安，舉從之。

translations.literal: Hao Yuan urged Xue Ju to join forces with Liang Shidu and the Turks to take Chang'an; Ju followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Yuan persuaded Xue Ju to ally with Liang Shidu and the Turks for a joint strike on Chang'an, and Ju agreed.

sentences.zh: 時啟民可汗之子咄苾，號莫賀咄設，建牙直五原之北，舉遣使與莫賀咄設謀入寇，莫賀咄設許之。

translations.literal: At this time Qibi, son of Qimin Khan, styled Moheduo She, had established his headquarters directly north of Wuyuan; Ju sent envoys to plot an incursion with Moheduo She, and Moheduo She agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Qibi, a son of Qimin Khan who styled himself Moheduo She, had pitched his camp just north of Wuyuan. Xue Ju sent envoys to arrange a joint raid, and Moheduo She consented.

sentences.zh: 唐王使都水監宇文歆賂莫賀咄設，且為陳利害，止其出兵，又說莫賀咄設遣張長遜入朝，以五原之地歸之中國，莫賀咄設並從之。
