translations.literal: The Prince of Tang sent Director of Waterworks Yuwen Xin to bribe Moheduo She, explain the advantages and disadvantages to him, and stop his marching out; he also urged Moheduo She to send Zhang Changsun to court and restore the lands of Wuyuan to China; Moheduo She assented to all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tang dispatched Yuwen Xin, Director of Waterworks, to bribe Moheduo She, spell out the stakes, and dissuade him from marching. Xin also persuaded Moheduo She to send Zhang Changsun to court and return Wuyuan to China—all of which Moheduo She accepted.

sentences.zh: 已卯，武都、宕渠、五原等郡皆降，王即以長遜為五原太守。

translations.literal: On the day Jimao, the commanderies Wudu, Dangqu, Wuyuan, and others all surrendered; the Prince appointed Changsun Administrator of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On Jimao, Wudu, Dangqu, Wuyuan, and other commanderies submitted. The Prince of Tang immediately made Zhang Changsun administrator of Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 長遜又詐為詔書與莫賀咄設，示知其謀。

translations.literal: Changsun also forged an imperial edict for Moheduo She, showing that their plot was known.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changsun also forged an imperial edict addressed to Moheduo She to let him know their scheme had been exposed.

sentences.zh: 莫賀咄設乃拒舉、師都等，不納其使。

translations.literal: Moheduo She thereupon rejected Ju, Shidu, and the others and refused to receive their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Moheduo She then turned Xue Ju and Liang Shidu away and refused their envoys entry.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，世子建成等還長安。

translations.literal: On the day Wuxu, Heir Apparent Li Jiancheng and the others returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On Wuxu, Heir Apparent Li Jiancheng and his forces returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 東都號令不出四門，人無固志，朝議郎段世弘等謀應西師。

translations.literal: In the Eastern Capital, orders could not pass beyond the four gates; the people had no fixed loyalty; Court Gentleman for Consultation Duan Shihong and others plotted to respond to the western army.
translations.idiomatic: Authority in the Eastern Capital barely extended beyond the city gates, morale was uncertain, and Court Gentleman for Consultation Duan Shihong and others plotted to cooperate with the western forces.

sentences.zh: 會西師已還，乃遣人招李密，期以己亥夜納之。

translations.literal: It happened that the western army had already returned, so they sent men to summon Li Mi, fixing the night of Jihai for him to be admitted.
translations.idiomatic: By then the western army had already withdrawn, so they sent to Li Mi and set the night of Jihai for him to be let in.

sentences.zh: 事覺，越王命王世充討誅之。

translations.literal: The plot was discovered; the Prince of Yue ordered Wang Shichong to suppress and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: The conspiracy was discovered, and the Prince of Yue sent Wang Shichong to stamp it out.

sentences.zh: 密聞城中已定，乃還。

translations.literal: Mi heard the city was already pacified and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that affairs in the city had been settled, Li Mi turned back.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及擁眾十餘萬，據有六宮，自奉養一如煬帝。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji held a following of more than one hundred thousand, occupied the Six Palaces, and maintained himself in the same style as Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Huaji commanded a host of more than one hundred thousand, occupied the Six Palaces, and lived in the same imperial style as Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 每於帳中南面坐，人有白事者，嘿然不對；

translations.literal: Each day he sat facing south in his tent; when men reported affairs to him, he remained silent and made no reply;
translations.idiomatic: Each day he sat facing south in his tent; when subordinates came to report business, he would sit in silence and say nothing;

sentences.zh: 下牙，方取啟狀與唐奉義、牛方裕、薛世良、張愷等參決之。

translations.literal: Only after leaving the audience did he take memorials and consult Tang Fengyi, Niu Fangyu, Xue Shiliang, Zhang Kai, and others to decide them.
translations.idiomatic: only after leaving the audience tent did he take up petitions and discuss them with Tang Fengyi, Niu Fangyu, Xue Shiliang, Zhang Kai, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 以少主浩付尚書省，令衛士十餘人守之，遣令史取其畫敕，百官不復朝參。

translations.literal: He handed the Young Lord Hao over to the Ministry of State and had more than ten guards watch him, sent clerks to fetch his written edicts, and the officials no longer attended court audience.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the young Lord Hao at the Ministry of State under guard by a dozen warriors, had clerks fetch his signatures for edicts, and ended regular court audiences for the officials.

sentences.zh: 至彭城，水路不通，復奪民車牛得二千兩，並載宮人珍寶；

translations.literal: When they reached Pengcheng the waterways were blocked; they again seized civilian carts and oxen, obtaining two thousand teams, and loaded palace women and treasures aboard;
translations.idiomatic: At Pengcheng the waterways were impassable, so they seized civilian carts and oxen—two thousand teams in all—to carry palace women and treasure;

sentences.zh: 其戈甲戎器，悉令軍士負之，道遠疲劇，軍士始怨。

translations.literal: As for armor and weapons of war, they had the soldiers carry them all; the road was long and the burden severe, and the soldiers began to murmur.
translations.idiomatic: while the soldiers were made to lug all the armor and weapons themselves. The long march exhausted them, and discontent spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 司馬德戡竊謂趙行樞曰：「君大謬，誤我！

translations.literal: Sima Dekan secretly said to Zhao Xingshu: "You have greatly erred and misled me!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Dekan whispered to Zhao Xingshu: "You were grievously wrong—you misled me!

sentences.zh: 當今撥亂，必藉英賢；

translations.literal: In today's age of settling disorder, one must rely on heroic talent;
translations.idiomatic: To set the realm right in times like these, you need a man of real gifts;

sentences.zh: 化及庸暗，群小在側，事將必敗，若之何？」

translations.literal: Huaji is mediocre and obtuse, with petty men at his side—the enterprise is bound to fail; what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Huaji is dull and petty-minded, with sycophants at his elbow. This venture is doomed—what are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 行樞曰：「在我等耳，廢之何難！」

translations.literal: Xingshu said: "It lies with us—how hard can it be to depose him!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingshu said: "That is up to us. Deposing him would not be hard!"

sentences.zh: 初，化及既得政，賜司馬德戡爵溫國公，加光祿大夫；

translations.literal: Earlier, after Huaji had seized power, he enfeoffed Sima Dekan as Duke of Wen with the additional title Grand Master for Splendid Happiness;
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji first took power he had enfeoffed Dekan as Duke of Wen and promoted him to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness;

sentences.zh: 以其專統驍果，心忌之。

translations.literal: Because Dekan exclusively commanded the crack troops, Huaji was jealous at heart.
translations.idiomatic: but he resented Dekan's sole command over the crack troops.

sentences.zh: 後數日，化及署諸將分配士卒，以德戡為禮部尚書，外示美遷，實奪其兵柄。

translations.literal: Several days later, as Huaji appointed the various generals to distribute the soldiers, he made Dekan Minister of Rites—outwardly an honorable transfer, in truth stripping him of military command.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later, as Huaji assigned generals to distribute the troops, he named Dekan Minister of Rites—a promotion in name that stripped him of real military power.

sentences.zh: 德戡由是憤怨，所獲賞賜，皆以賂智及；

translations.literal: Dekan was thus filled with resentment and anger; whatever rewards he received he used to bribe Zhiji;
translations.idiomatic: Dekan, furious, funneled every reward he received to bribe Zhiji;

sentences.zh: 智及為之言，乃使之將後軍萬餘人以從。

translations.literal: Zhiji spoke on his behalf, and Huaji then had him lead the rear guard of more than ten thousand men to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji interceded for him, and Huaji allowed him to command the rear guard of more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 於是德戡、行樞與諸將李本、尹正卿、宇文導師等謀以後軍襲殺化及，更立德戡為主；

translations.literal: Thereupon Dekan, Xingshu, and the generals Li Ben, Yin Zhengqing, Yuwen Daoshi, and others plotted to use the rear guard to surprise and kill Huaji and set up Dekan as leader;
translations.idiomatic: Dekan, Xingshu, and generals including Li Ben, Yin Zhengqing, and Yuwen Daoshi then plotted to use the rear guard to assassinate Huaji and install Dekan as leader;

sentences.zh: 遣人詣孟海公，結為外助；

translations.literal: They sent men to Meng Haigong to secure outside support;
translations.idiomatic: they sent envoys to Meng Haigong to secure outside aid;

sentences.zh: 遷延未發，待海公報。

translations.literal: They delayed and did not act, awaiting Haigong's reply.
translations.idiomatic: and held back, waiting for Haigong's answer.

sentences.zh: 許弘仁、張愷知之，以告化及。

translations.literal: Xu Hongren and Zhang Kai learned of it and reported it to Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hongren and Zhang Kai found out and told Huaji.

sentences.zh: 化及遣宇文士及陽為遊獵，至後軍，德戡不知事露，出營迎謁，因執之。

translations.literal: Huaji sent Yuwen Shiji under the pretense of a hunting excursion to the rear guard; Dekan, not knowing the plot was exposed, came out of camp to greet him and was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji sent Yuwen Shiji on a feigned hunting outing to the rear guard. Dekan, unaware the plot had leaked, came out to greet him and was arrested.

sentences.zh: 化及讓之曰：「與公戮力共定海內，出於萬死。

translations.literal: Huaji reproached him, saying: "You and I exerted our strength together to settle the realm, escaping death by a hairbreadth.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji upbraided him: "You and I risked death together to seize the empire.

sentences.zh: 今始事成，方願共守富貴，公又何反也？」

translations.literal: Now that it has just succeeded, I looked to share wealth and rank with you—why would you rebel again?"
translations.idiomatic: We have only just succeeded, and I meant for us to share riches and power—why turn against me now?"

sentences.zh: 德戡曰：「本殺昏主，苦其淫虐；

translations.literal: Dekan said: "We originally killed the benighted sovereign because we suffered under his wanton tyranny;
translations.idiomatic: Dekan said: "We killed the tyrant because we could not bear his excesses;

sentences.zh: 推立足下，而又甚之；

translations.literal: We raised you up, yet you have surpassed him in this;
translations.idiomatic: we put you in power, and you have been worse;

sentences.zh: 逼於物情，不獲已也。」

translations.literal: Pressed by the temper of affairs, I had no choice."
translations.idiomatic: driven by the way things stand, I had no choice."

sentences.zh: 化及縊殺之，並殺其支黨十餘人。

translations.literal: Huaji strangled him to death and also killed more than ten of his partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji had him strangled and executed more than a dozen of his accomplices.

sentences.zh: 孟海公畏化及之強，帥眾具牛酒迎之。

translations.literal: Meng Haigong feared Huaji's strength and led his followers with oxen and wine to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Haigong, intimidated by Huaji's power, marched out with oxen and wine to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 李密據鞏洛以拒化及，化及不得西，引兵向東郡，東郡通守王軌以城降之。

translations.literal: Li Mi held Gongluo to resist Huaji; Huaji could not go west and led his army toward Dong Commandery; Chief Secretary Wang Gui of Dong Commandery surrendered the city to him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi held the Gong-Luo line against Huaji, blocking his westward advance. Huaji turned toward Dong Commandery, where Chief Secretary Wang Gui surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，李密將井陘王君廓帥眾來降。

translations.literal: On the day Xinchou, Li Mi's general Wang Junkuo, Prince of Jingxing, led his followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On Xinchou, Wang Junkuo, Li Mi's general and Prince of Jingxing, submitted with his followers.

sentences.zh: 君廓本群盜，有眾數千人，與賊帥韋寶、鄧豹合軍虞鄉，唐王與李密俱遣使招之。

translations.literal: Junkuo had originally been a bandit leader with several thousand followers; he joined forces with the bandit chiefs Wei Bao and Deng Bao at Yuxiang; both the Prince of Tang and Li Mi sent envoys to recruit him.
translations.idiomatic: Junkuo had begun as a bandit chief with several thousand men and had joined Wei Bao and Deng Bao at Yuxiang. Both the Prince of Tang and Li Mi sent envoys to win him over.

sentences.zh: 寶、豹欲從唐王，君廓偽與之同，乘其無備，襲擊，破之，奪其輜重，奔李密；

translations.literal: Bao and Bao wished to follow the Prince of Tang; Junkuo pretended to agree with them, took them unawares in a surprise attack, defeated them, seized their baggage train, and fled to Li Mi;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bao and Deng Bao favored the Prince of Tang, but Junkuo feigned agreement, struck when they were unprepared, routed them, seized their baggage, and fled to Li Mi;

sentences.zh: 密不禮之，復來降，拜上柱國，假河內太守。

translations.literal: Mi did not treat him with courtesy; he came to surrender again and was appointed Senior Pillar of State and provisional Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi snubbed him, so he submitted again and was made Senior Pillar of State and acting Administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑即皇帝位，置百官，准梁室故事。

translations.literal: Xiao Xian immediately assumed the imperial throne, established the full roster of officials, and followed the precedents of the Liang house.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian took the throne, installed a full bureaucracy, and modeled his court on the Liang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 謚其從父琮為孝靖皇帝，祖巖為河間忠烈王，父璿為文憲王，封董景珍等功臣七人皆為王。

translations.literal: He posthumously titled his father's younger brother Cong as Emperor Xiaojing, his grandfather Yan as Loyal and Fierce Prince of Hejian, his father Xuan as Prince Wenxian, and enfeoffed seven meritorious men including Dong Jingzhen as kings.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored his father's younger brother Cong as Emperor Xiaojing, his grandfather Yan as Loyal and Fierce Prince of Hejian, his father Xuan as Prince Wenxian, and enfeoffed seven merit-holders including Dong Jingzhen as kings.

sentences.zh: 遣宋王楊道生擊南郡，下之，徒都江陵，修復園廟。

translations.literal: He dispatched Prince of Song Yang Daosheng to attack Nan Commandery, took it, moved the capital to Jiangling, and restored the imperial gardens and ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Prince of Song Yang Daosheng against Nan Commandery, captured it, moved the capital to Jiangling, and restored the imperial gardens and ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 引岑文本為中書侍郎，使典文翰，委以機密。

translations.literal: He brought in Cen Wenben as Vice Director of the Secretariat, had him oversee documents, and entrusted him with confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in Cen Wenben as Vice Director of the Secretariat to manage official documents and entrusted him with state secrets.

sentences.zh: 又使魯王張繡徇嶺南，隋將張鎮周、王仁壽等拒之；

translations.literal: He also sent Prince of Lu Zhang Xiu to campaign in Lingnan; Sui generals Zhang Zhenzhou, Wang Renshou, and others resisted them;
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Prince of Lu Zhang Xiu into Lingnan, where Sui generals Zhang Zhenzhou and Wang Renshou held them off.

sentences.zh: 既而聞煬帝遇弒，皆降於銑。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on learning that Emperor Yang had been assassinated, they all surrendered to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When they later heard that Emperor Yang had been murdered, they all submitted to Xiao Xian.

sentences.zh: 欽州刺史寧長真亦以鬱林、始安之地附於銑。

translations.literal: Prefect of Qinzhou Ning Changzhen also submitted the lands of Yulin and Shian to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Changzhen, prefect of Qinzhou, also attached the Yulin and Shian territories to Xiao Xian.

sentences.zh: 漢陽太守馮盎以蒼梧、高涼、珠崖、番禺之地附於林士弘。

translations.literal: Administrator of Hanyang Feng Ang submitted the lands of Cangwu, Gaoliang, Zhuya, and Panyu to Lin Shihong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ang, administrator of Hanyang, submitted Cangwu, Gaoliang, Zhuya, and Panyu to Lin Shihong.

sentences.zh: 銑、士弘各遣人招交趾太守丘和，和不從。

translations.literal: Xian and Shihong each sent men to recruit Administrator of Jiaozhi Qiu He; He would not follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian and Lin Shihong each sent envoys to win over Qiu He, administrator of Jiaozhi, but He refused both.

sentences.zh: 銑遣寧長真帥嶺南兵自海道攻和，和欲出迎之，司法書佐高士廉說和曰：「長真兵數雖多，懸軍遠至，不能持久，城中勝兵足以當之，奈何望風受制於人！」

translations.literal: Xian sent Ning Changzhen to lead Lingnan troops by sea route to attack He; He wished to go out to welcome them; Judicial Secretary Assistant Gao Shilian urged He, saying: "Changzhen's troops are numerous, but an army far from home cannot endure long; the able soldiers in the city are enough to oppose them—why submit at the first sight of the enemy!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian sent Ning Changzhen with Lingnan troops by sea against Qiu He, who intended to go out and receive them. Gao Shilian, a judicial secretary, urged him: "Changzhen may have many men, but an army this far from home cannot keep it up. Our able fighters in the city are enough to meet them—why surrender at the first wind?"

sentences.zh: 和從之，以士廉為軍司馬，將水陸諸軍逆擊，破之，長真僅以身免，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: He followed this advice, made Shilian army aide-de-camp, led land and river forces in a counterattack, defeated them; Changzhen barely escaped with his life, and all his followers were captured.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed, made Gao Shilian his army marshal, and led land and river forces in a counterattack. Changzhen barely escaped; his entire force was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 既而有驍果自江都至，得煬帝凶問，亦以郡附於銑。

translations.literal: Soon afterward crack troops arrived from Jiangdu; learning of Emperor Yang's death, they also submitted the commandery to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Later, crack troops from Jiangdu arrived, heard news of Emperor Yang's murder, and also submitted the commandery to Xiao Xian.

sentences.zh: 士廉，勱之子也。

translations.literal: Shilian was the son of Li.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shilian was the son of Gao Li.

sentences.zh: 始安郡丞李襲志，遷哲之孫也，隋末，散家財，募士得三千人，以保郡城；

translations.literal: Assistant Prefect of Shian Commandery Li Xizhi was the grandson of Qianzhe; at the end of Sui, he dispersed his family wealth, recruited soldiers and obtained three thousand men to protect the commandery city;
translations.idiomatic: Li Xizhi, assistant prefect of Shian, was a grandson of Qianzhe. At the end of the Sui he spent his family fortune to raise three thousand men and hold the commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑、林士弘、曹武徹迭來攻之，皆不克。

translations.literal: Xiao Xian, Lin Shihong, and Cao Wuche attacked in succession and none could overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian, Lin Shihong, and Cao Wuche attacked him in turn and failed to take the city.

sentences.zh: 聞煬帝遇弒，帥吏民臨三日。

translations.literal: On hearing that Emperor Yang had been assassinated, he led officials and people in mourning for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Emperor Yang had been murdered, he led officials and commoners in three days of mourning.

sentences.zh: 或說襲志曰：「公中州貴族，久臨鄙郡，華、夷悅服。

translations.literal: Someone urged Xizhi, saying: "You are a noble of the Central Plains, long governing this remote commandery; Chinese and barbarians alike are pleased and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Xizhi: "You are a Central Plains aristocrat who has long governed this outlying commandery. Chinese and indigenous peoples alike respect you.

sentences.zh: 今隋室無主，海內鼎沸，以公威惠，號令嶺表，尉佗之業可坐致也。」

translations.literal: Now the Sui house has no master, the realm seethes like a cauldron—with your prestige and benevolence you could command Lingnan and the achievement of Zhao Tuo could be obtained without effort."
translations.idiomatic: The Sui is headless and the empire boils with unrest. With your authority and goodwill you could rule all of Lingnan and replicate Zhao Tuo's kingdom almost without lifting a finger."

sentences.zh: 襲志怒曰：「吾世繼忠貞，今江都雖覆，宗社尚存，尉佗狂僭，何足慕也！」

translations.literal: Xizhi angrily said: "My family has for generations inherited loyalty and steadfastness; though Jiangdu has fallen, the altars of state still stand—Zhao Tuo's reckless usurpation is nothing to admire!"
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi raged: "My house has served in loyalty for generations. Jiangdu may have fallen, but the dynasty endures. Zhao Tuo was a reckless usurper—what is there to envy!"

sentences.zh: 欲斬說者，眾乃不敢言。

translations.literal: He wished to behead the adviser, and the crowd then dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: He nearly had the man executed, and no one dared raise the subject again.

sentences.zh: 堅守二年，外無聲援，城陷，為銑所虜，銑以為工部尚書，檢校桂州總管。

translations.literal: He held firm for two years; with no outside support the city fell, he was captured by Xian, and Xian made him Minister of Public Works and acting Grand Commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He held out for two years without outside aid until the city fell. Xiao Xian took him captive, made him Minister of Public Works, and put him in charge as acting Grand Commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 於是東自九江，西抵三峽，南盡交趾，北距漢川，銑皆有之，勝兵四十餘萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon, from Jiujiang in the east to the Three Gorges in the west, from Jiaozhi in the south to Hanchuan in the north, Xian held it all, with more than four hundred thousand able soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian now controlled everything from Jiujiang in the east to the Three Gorges in the west, from Jiaozhi in the south to the Han River frontier in the north—more than four hundred thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 煬帝凶問至長安，唐王哭之慟，曰：「吾北面事人，失道不能救，敢忘哀乎！」

translations.literal: When news of Emperor Yang's death reached Chang'an, the Prince of Tang wept bitterly and said: "I served another as subject facing north; having failed in the Way I could not rescue him—how dare I forget grief!"
translations.idiomatic: When word of Emperor Yang's death reached Chang'an, the Prince of Tang wept bitterly and said: "I served him as a subject and could not save him when the realm went astray—how can I fail to mourn?"

sentences.zh: 五月，山南撫慰使馬元規擊朱粲於冠軍，破之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Pacification Commissioner of Shannan Ma Yuangui attacked Zhu Can at Guanjun and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Shannan Pacification Commissioner Ma Yuangui defeated Zhu Can at Guanjun.

sentences.zh: 王德仁既殺房彥澡，李密遣徐世勣討之。

translations.literal: After Wang Deren had killed Fang Yanzao, Li Mi dispatched Xu Shiji to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Deren killed Fang Yanzao, Li Mi sent Xu Shiji against him.

sentences.zh: 德仁兵敗，甲寅，與武安通守袁子幹皆來降，詔以德仁為鄴郡太守。

translations.literal: Deren's army was defeated; on the day Jiayin he and Chief Secretary of Wu'an Yuan Zigan both came to surrender; an edict appointed Deren Administrator of Ye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Deren was defeated. On Jiayin he and Yuan Zigan, chief secretary of Wu'an, submitted together; Deren was appointed administrator of Ye Commandery.

sentences.zh: 戊午，隋恭帝禪位於唐，遜居代邸。

translations.literal: On the day Wuwu, Emperor Gong of Sui abdicated the throne to Tang and retired to the residence at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: On Wuwu, Emperor Gong of Sui abdicated to the Tang and withdrew to the residence at Dai.

sentences.zh: 甲子，唐王即皇帝位於太極殿，遣刑部尚書蕭造告天於南郊，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On the day Jiazi, the Prince of Tang ascended the imperial throne in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, sent Minister of Punishments Xiao Zao to announce Heaven at the Southern Suburbs, granted a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: On Jiazi, the Prince of Tang took the throne in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, dispatched Minister of Punishments Xiao Zao to report to Heaven at the Southern Suburbs, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted a new reign title.

sentences.zh: 罷郡，置州，以太守為剌史。

translations.literal: Commanderies were abolished and prefectures established; grand administrators were made prefects.
translations.idiomatic: The government abolished commanderies in favor of prefectures and renamed grand administrators as prefects.

sentences.zh: 推五運為土德，色尚黃。

translations.literal: The Five Movements were calculated as the virtue of Earth, and the color yellow was honored.
translations.idiomatic: The court identified the dynasty with the Earth phase of the Five Movements and adopted yellow as the imperial color.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝凶問至東都，戊辰，留守官奉越王即皇帝位，大赦，改元皇泰。

translations.literal: When news of Emperor Yang of Sui's death reached the Eastern Capital, on the day Wuchen the officials left to guard the city installed the Prince of Yue as emperor, granted a general amnesty, and changed the reign title to Huangtai.
translations.idiomatic: After word of Emperor Yang of Sui's death reached the Eastern Capital, on Wuchen the garrison officials enthroned the Prince of Yue, proclaimed a general amnesty, and declared the reign era Huangtai.

sentences.zh: 是日於朝堂宣旨，以時鐘金革，公私皆即日大祥。

translations.literal: That same day an edict was proclaimed in the audience hall: because the times called for bells and weapons, both public and private mourning would observe the full mourning rite that very day.
translations.idiomatic: That day an edict was read in the audience hall declaring that, with war upon them, public and private mourning alike would enter the full mourning period immediately.

sentences.zh: 追謚大行曰明皇帝，廟號世祖；

translations.literal: The late Emperor was posthumously titled Emperor Ming, with temple name Shizu;
translations.idiomatic: The deceased sovereign was posthumously honored as Emperor Ming, temple name Shizu;

sentences.zh: 追尊元德太子曰成皇帝，廟號世宗。

translations.literal: The Yuande Crown Prince was posthumously honored as Emperor Cheng, with temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuande Crown Prince was posthumously elevated to Emperor Cheng, temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 尊母劉良娣為皇太后。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Liu Liangdi, was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He honored his mother, Lady Liu Liangdi, as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 以段達為納言、陳國公，王世充為納言、鄭國公，元文都為內史令、魯國公，皇甫無逸為兵部尚書、杞國公，又以盧楚為內史令，郭文懿為內史侍郎，趙長文為黃門侍郎，共掌朝政，時人號「七貴」。

translations.literal: Duan Da was made Chief Counselor and Duke of Chen; Wang Shichong was made Chief Counselor and Duke of Zheng; Yuan Wendu was made Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Lu; Huangfu Wuyi was made Minister of War and Duke of Qi; Lu Chu was also made Director of the Secretariat; Guo Wenyi was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Zhao Changwen was made Vice Director of the Chancellery. Together they controlled court governance, and people of the time called them the "Seven Worthies."
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da was appointed Chief Counselor and Duke of Chen; Wang Shichong Chief Counselor and Duke of Zheng; Yuan Wendu Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Lu; Huangfu Wuyi Minister of War and Duke of Qi; Lu Chu also became Director of the Secretariat; Guo Wenyi Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Zhao Changwen Vice Director of the Chancellery. These seven jointly ran the government, and contemporaries dubbed them the "Seven Worthies."

sentences.zh: 皇泰主眉目如畫，溫厚仁愛，風格儼然。

translations.literal: The Huangtai sovereign's brows and eyes were like a painting; he was warm, generous, and loving, with a bearing of solemn dignity.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangtai sovereign had features fine as a painted portrait—gentle, kind, and gracious, with a naturally dignified air.

sentences.zh: 辛未，突厥始畢可汗遣骨咄祿特勒來，宴之於太極殿，奏九部樂。

translations.literal: On the day Xinwei, Shibi Khan of the Turks sent Gudulu the Tegin; he was feasted in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and the nine-part music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On Xinwei, Shibi Khan of the Turks sent Gudulu the Tegin, who was entertained in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate while the nine-part court music was played.

sentences.zh: 時中國人避亂者多入突厥，突厥強盛，東自契丹、室韋，西盡吐谷渾、高昌，諸國皆臣之，控弦百餘萬。

translations.literal: At this time many Chinese fleeing turmoil entered the Turks; the Turks were powerful—from the Khitan and Shiwei in the east to Tuyuhun and Gaochang in the west, all states submitted to them, and they could field more than a million bowmen.
translations.idiomatic: Many Chinese refugees fleeing the chaos had by then fled into Turkic territory. The Turks were at their height: from the Khitan and Shiwei in the east to Tuyuhun and Gaochang in the west, neighboring states acknowledged their supremacy, and they commanded more than a million mounted archers.

sentences.zh: 帝以初起資其兵馬，前後餉遺，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: The Emperor, at the beginning of his rise, had relied on their horses and troops; gifts sent before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan had depended on Turkic horses and soldiers in his first campaigns, and the gifts of tribute sent before and since were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 突厥恃功驕倨，每遣使者至長安，多暴橫，帝優容之。

translations.literal: The Turks, relying on their merit, were arrogant and overbearing; whenever they sent envoys to Chang'an they were often violent and domineering, yet the Emperor indulged them.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by their services, the Turks grew haughty; their envoys to Chang'an were often brutal and overbearing, yet Li Yuan treated them with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 壬申，命裴寂、劉文靜等修定律令。

translations.literal: On the day Renshen, he ordered Pei Ji, Liu Wenjing, and others to revise laws and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: On Renshen, Li Yuan ordered Pei Ji, Liu Wenjing, and others to compile and revise the laws and statutes.

sentences.zh: 置國子、太學、四門生，合三百餘員，郡縣學亦各置生員。

translations.literal: Students were established for the Directorate, Imperial University, and Four Gates schools, totaling more than three hundred; commandery and county schools also each established student quotas.
translations.idiomatic: The court enrolled more than three hundred students across the Directorate, Imperial University, and Four Gates schools, and commandery and county schools likewise received their own student quotas.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲戌朔，以趙公世民為尚書令，黃台公瑗為刑部侍郎，相國府長史裴寂為右僕射、知政事，司馬劉文靜為納言，司錄竇威為內史令，李綱為禮部尚書、參掌選事，掾殷開山為吏部侍郎，屬趙慈景為兵部侍郎，韋義節為禮部侍郎，主簿陳叔達、博陵崔民幹並為黃門侍郎，唐儉為內史侍郎，錄事參軍裴晞為尚書右丞；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day of the month Jiaxu, the Duke of Zhao Shimin was made Director of the Department of State Affairs; the Duke of Huangtai Yuan was made Vice Minister of Punishments; Pei Ji, chief secretary of the chancellor's office, was made Right Vice Director and put in charge of government affairs; Liu Wenjing, chief administrator, was made Chief Counselor; Dou Wei, chief recorder, was made Director of the Secretariat; Li Gang was made Minister of Rites and given charge of selection affairs; Yin Kaishan, a staff officer, was made Vice Minister of Personnel; Zhao Cijing, an aide, was made Vice Minister of War; Wei Yijie was made Vice Minister of Rites; Chen Shuda, chief clerk, and Cui Mingan of Boling were both made Vice Directors of the Chancellery; Tang Jian was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Pei Xi, recording officer, was made Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the first day Jiaxu, Li Shimin, Duke of Zhao, was named Director of the Department of State Affairs; Yuan, Duke of Huangtai, Vice Minister of Punishments; Pei Ji, chief secretary of the chancellor's office, Right Vice Director with charge of government affairs; Liu Wenjing, Chief Counselor; Dou Wei, Director of the Secretariat; Li Gang, Minister of Rites with responsibility for appointments; Yin Kaishan, Vice Minister of Personnel; Zhao Cijing, Vice Minister of War; Wei Yijie, Vice Minister of Rites; Chen Shuda and Cui Mingan of Boling, both Vice Directors of the Chancellery; Tang Jian, Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Pei Xi, Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs;

sentences.zh: 以隋民部尚書蕭瑀為內史令，禮部尚書竇璡為戶部尚書，蔣公屈突通為兵部尚書，長安令獨孤懷恩為工部尚書。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu, former Sui Minister of the People, was made Director of the Secretariat; Dou Jin, Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Revenue; Qu Tu Tong, Duke of Jiang, was made Minister of War; and Dugu Huai'en, magistrate of Chang'an, was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu, former Sui Minister of the People, became Director of the Secretariat; Dou Jin moved from Minister of Rites to Minister of Revenue; Qu Tu Tong, Duke of Jiang, was made Minister of War; and Dugu Huai'en, magistrate of Chang'an, Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 瑗，上之從子；

translations.literal: Yuan was the Emperor's nephew, the son of his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was Li Yuan's nephew, a son of his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 懷恩，舅子也。

translations.literal: Huai'en was a nephew on the maternal side.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was a nephew through Li Yuan's wife's family.

sentences.zh: 上待裴寂特厚，群臣無與為比，賞賜服玩，不可勝紀；

translations.literal: The Emperor treated Pei Ji with exceptional favor, unmatched among the ministers; rewards of robes and curios were beyond counting;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan favored Pei Ji above all other ministers; the gifts of robes and luxuries lavished on him were beyond counting;

sentences.zh: 命尚書奉御日以御膳賜寂，視朝必引與同坐，入閣則延之臥內；

translations.literal: He ordered the palace provisioners to send imperial meals to Ji daily; at audience he always had him sit beside him, and when entering the private quarters he invited him into the bedchamber;
translations.idiomatic: He had the palace kitchen send Pei Ji the imperial table daily, always seated him at his side during audiences, and when retiring to the inner quarters welcomed him into his sleeping chamber;

sentences.zh: 言無不從，稱為裴監而不名。

translations.literal: Nothing he said was refused; he was addressed as Supervisor Pei without using his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji's word was law, and the Emperor addressed him as Supervisor Pei rather than by name.

sentences.zh: 委蕭瑀以庶政，事無大小，莫不關掌。

translations.literal: He entrusted routine governance to Xiao Yu; nothing great or small escaped his oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan entrusted day-to-day administration to Xiao Yu, who handled affairs large and small alike.

sentences.zh: 瑀亦孜孜盡力，繩違舉過，人皆憚之，毀之者眾，終不自理。

translations.literal: Yu also toiled diligently, correcting violations and citing faults; everyone feared him, and though many slandered him, he never defended himself to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu worked tirelessly, enforcing discipline and exposing misconduct; officials feared him, slander against him was widespread, yet he never once pleaded his own case.

sentences.zh: 上嘗有敕而內史不時宣行，上責其遲，瑀對曰：「大業之世，內史宣敕，或前後相違，有司不知所從，其易在前，其難在後；

translations.literal: Once the Emperor issued an edict but the Secretariat did not promulgate it in time; the Emperor blamed them for the delay. Yu replied: "In the Daye reign, when the Secretariat promulgated edicts, some contradicted earlier ones, and the responsible offices did not know which to follow—the ease lay in the front, the difficulty in what came after;
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Yuan issued an edict that the Secretariat failed to promulgate promptly, and he rebuked them for the delay. Xiao Yu answered, "Under the Daye reign, edicts from the Secretariat often contradicted one another, leaving officials unsure which to obey—the first was easy to issue, the later ones hard to reconcile;

sentences.zh: 臣在省日久，備見其事。

translations.literal: Your servant has long served in the Secretariat and has seen this fully.
translations.idiomatic: I have served in the Secretariat for many years and witnessed this myself.

sentences.zh: 今王業經始，事系安危，遠方有疑，恐失機會，故臣每受一敕必勘審，使與前敕不違，始敢宣行；

translations.literal: Now the royal enterprise has just begun and affairs bear on safety and peril; if distant regions harbor doubts, we may lose opportunities—therefore your servant, upon receiving each edict, must examine it to ensure it does not conflict with earlier edicts before daring to promulgate it;
translations.idiomatic: Now that the dynasty is newly founded and every order touches on survival, any inconsistency could breed doubt in distant provinces and cost us our moment—so I review each edict against earlier ones and only promulgate it when they align;

sentences.zh: 稽緩之愆，實由於此。」

translations.literal: The fault of delay in fact stems from this."
translations.idiomatic: That is the true reason for the delay."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿用心如是，吾復何憂！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "With such care on your part, what have I to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan said, "If you attend to matters with such care, what have I to fear!"

sentences.zh: 初，帝遣馬元規慰撫山南，南陽郡丞河東呂子臧獨據郡不從；

translations.literal: Earlier, the Emperor had sent Ma Yuangui to reassure and pacify the region south of the mountains; Lu Zicang of Hedong, aide to the Nanyang commandery, alone held the commandery and would not submit;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Yuan had dispatched Ma Yuangui to pacify the lands south of the mountains, but Lu Zicang of Hedong, deputy magistrate of Nanyang commandery, held the district alone and refused to submit;

sentences.zh: 元規遣使數輩諭之，皆為子臧所殺。

translations.literal: Yuangui sent several envoys to instruct him, and all were killed by Zicang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuangui sent envoy after envoy to reason with him, and Lu Zicang killed them all.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝遇弒，子臧發喪成禮，然後請降；

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was assassinated, Zicang conducted mourning rites and only then requested surrender;
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang was murdered, Lu Zicang properly observed the mourning rites and only then offered to surrender;

sentences.zh: 拜鄧州刺史，封南郡公。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Dengzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Dengzhou and created Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 廢大業律令，頒新格。

translations.literal: The Daye laws and statutes were abolished and new regulations were promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: The court abolished the Daye-era laws and issued a new legal code.

sentences.zh: 上每視事，自稱名，引貴臣同榻而坐。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor conducted affairs of state, he used his personal name and invited eminent ministers to sit on the same couch with him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Li Yuan held court, he addressed himself by his personal name and had senior ministers share his couch.

sentences.zh: 劉文靜諫曰：「昔王導有言：『若太陽俯同萬物，使群生何以仰照！』

translations.literal: Liu Wenjing remonstrated, saying: "In former times Wang Dao had a saying: 'If the sun stoops to the level of all things, how shall the myriad beings look up to its light!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenjing admonished him: "Wang Dao once said, 'If the sun lowers itself to the level of every creature, what will the people have to look up to!

sentences.zh: 今貴賤失位，非常久之道。」

translations.literal: Today noble and base have lost their proper places—this is not a way to endure for long."
translations.idiomatic: High and low have lost their proper stations—such a practice cannot last."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「昔漢光武與嚴子陵共寢，子陵加足於帝腹。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "In former times Emperor Guangwu of Han slept with Yan Ziling, and Ziling placed his foot on the Emperor's belly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan replied, "Emperor Guangwu of Han once shared a bed with Yan Ziling, who even rested his foot on the emperor's stomach.

sentences.zh: 今諸公皆名德舊齒，平生親友，宿昔之歡，何可忘也。

translations.literal: Today these lords are all men of renown and virtue, old in years, lifelong friends—how can the joys of days past be forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: These men are all old friends of honored name and long standing—how can I forget the companionship of earlier days?

sentences.zh: 公勿以為嫌！」

translations.literal: Sir, do not take offense at this!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not take it amiss!"

sentences.zh: 戊寅，隋安陽令呂鈱以相州來降，以為相州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day Wuyin, Lu Yin, magistrate of Anyang under Sui, surrendered Xiangzhou; he was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On Wuyin, Lu Yin, former Sui magistrate of Anyang, surrendered Xiangzhou and was appointed its prefect.

sentences.zh: 己卯，祔四親廟主。

translations.literal: On the day Jimao, the spirit tablets of the four immediate ancestors were enshrined in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On Jimao, the spirit tablets of the four immediate ancestors were installed in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 追尊皇高祖瀛州府君曰宣簡公；

translations.literal: The Emperor's great-great-grandfather, Lord of Yingzhou Prefecture, was posthumously honored as Duke Xuanjian;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan's great-great-grandfather, Lord of Yingzhou, was posthumously titled Duke Xuanjian;

sentences.zh: 皇曾祖司空曰懿王；

translations.literal: The Emperor's great-grandfather, Grand Minister of Works, was titled Prince Yi;
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather, former Grand Minister of Works, was honored as Prince Yi;

sentences.zh: 皇祖景王曰景皇帝，廟號太祖，祖妣曰景烈皇后；

translations.literal: The Emperor's grandfather, Prince Jing, was titled Emperor Jing, with temple name Taizu; his grandmother was titled Empress Jinglie;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Prince Jing was posthumously elevated to Emperor Jing, temple name Taizu, and his grandmother to Empress Jinglie;

sentences.zh: 皇考元王曰元皇帝，廟號世祖，妣獨孤氏曰元貞皇后；

translations.literal: The Emperor's father, Prince Yuan, was titled Emperor Yuan, with temple name Shizu; his mother, of the Dugu clan, was titled Empress Yuanzhen;
translations.idiomatic: His father Prince Yuan became Emperor Yuan, temple name Shizu, and his mother of the Dugu clan was honored as Empress Yuanzhen;

sentences.zh: 追謚妃竇氏曰穆皇后。

translations.literal: Consort Dou was posthumously titled Empress Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Dou was posthumously honored as Empress Mu.

sentences.zh: 每歲祀昊天上帝、皇地示氏、神州地示氏，以景帝配，感生帝、明堂，以元帝配。

translations.literal: Each year in sacrifices to the August Heaven, the August Earth, and the August Earth of the Divine Land, Emperor Jing was paired; at the Hall of Enlightenment to the Lord of Life-Generation, Emperor Yuan was paired.
translations.idiomatic: In the annual rites to August Heaven, August Earth, and the Divine Land, Emperor Jing served as the paired ancestor; at the Hall of Enlightenment rites to the Lord of Life-Generation, Emperor Yuan was the paired ancestor.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，立世子建成為皇太子，趙公世民為秦王，齊公元吉為齊王，宗室黃瓜公白駒為平原王，蜀公孝基為永安王，柱國道玄為淮陽王，長平公叔良為長平王，鄭公神通為永康王，安吉公神符為襄邑王，柱國德良為新興王，上柱國博叉為隴西王，上柱國奉慈為勃海王。

translations.literal: On the day Gengchen, the heir Jiancheng was established as Crown Prince; the Duke of Zhao Shimin was made Prince of Qin; the Duke of Qi Yuanji was made Prince of Qi; the clansman Bai Ju, Duke of Huang-gua, was made Prince of Pingyuan; the Duke of Shu Xiaoji was made Prince of Yong'an; Daoxuan, pillar of state, was made Prince of Huaiyang; the Duke of Changping Shuliang was made Prince of Changping; the Duke of Zheng Shentong was made Prince of Yongkang; the Duke of Anji Shenfu was made Prince of Xiangyi; Deliang, pillar of state, was made Prince of Xingxing; Bocha, supreme pillar of state, was made Prince of Longxi; and Fengci, supreme pillar of state, was made Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: On Gengchen, Li Jiancheng was installed as Crown Prince; Li Shimin, Duke of Zhao, was created Prince of Qin; Li Yuanji, Duke of Qi, Prince of Qi; the clansman Bai Ju, Duke of Huang-gua, Prince of Pingyuan; Xiaoji, Duke of Shu, Prince of Yong'an; Daoxuan, Prince of Huaiyang; Shuliang, Duke of Changping, Prince of Changping; Shentong, Duke of Zheng, Prince of Yongkang; Shenfu, Duke of Anji, Prince of Xiangyi; Deliang, Prince of Xingxing; Bocha, Prince of Longxi; and Fengci, Prince of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 孝基、叔良、神符、德良，帝之從父弟；

translations.literal: Xiaoji, Shuliang, Shenfu, and Deliang were the Emperor's younger cousins, sons of paternal uncles;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoji, Shuliang, Shenfu, and Deliang were Li Yuan's younger male cousins;

sentences.zh: 博叉、奉慈，弟子；

translations.literal: Bocha and Fengci were sons of younger brothers;
translations.idiomatic: Bocha and Fengci were sons of Li Yuan's younger brothers;

sentences.zh: 道玄，從父兄子也。

translations.literal: Daoxuan was the son of an elder male cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxuan was the son of an elder male cousin on Li Yuan's father's side.

sentences.zh: 癸未，薛舉寇涇州。

translations.literal: On the day Guiwei, Xue Ju raided Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On Guiwei, Xue Ju invaded Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以秦王世民為元帥，將八總管兵以拒之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin Shimin was made supreme commander and led the troops of eight area commanders to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin, Prince of Qin, was appointed supreme commander and led the forces of eight area commanders to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 遣太僕卿宇文明達招慰山東，以永安王孝基為陝州總管。

translations.literal: Grandee of Splendid Happiness Yu Wenmingda was sent to summon and reassure the Shandong region; Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji was made area commander of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan dispatched Grandee of Splendid Happiness Yu Wenmingda to win over the Shandong region and appointed Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji area commander of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時天下未定，凡邊要之州，皆置總管府，以統數州之兵。

translations.literal: At this time the realm was not yet settled; wherever a frontier prefecture was strategically vital, an area commander's office was established to command the troops of several prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: With the empire still unsettled, strategically important frontier prefectures each received an area commander's headquarters to oversee the military forces of several prefectures.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，奉隋帝為酅國公。

translations.literal: On the day Yiyou, the Sui emperor was honored as Duke of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: On Yiyou, the former Sui emperor was enfeoffed as Duke of Xi.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「近世以來，時運遷革，前代親族，莫不誅夷。

translations.literal: An edict said: "In recent generations, as the times shifted and dynasties changed, the kinsmen of former dynasties were without exception exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "In recent ages, as fortune turned and dynasties fell, the royal kin of each outgoing house were slaughtered without exception.

sentences.zh: 興亡之效，豈伊人力！

translations.literal: The effect of rise and fall—how could it depend on human effort alone!
translations.idiomatic: The rise and fall of states—surely that is not merely a matter of human will!

sentences.zh: 其隋蔡王智積等子孫，並付所司，量才選用。」

translations.literal: The descendants of the Sui Prince of Cai Zhiji and others shall all be handed over to the responsible offices to be selected and employed according to their talents."
translations.idiomatic: Let the descendants of Sui's Prince of Cai, Zhiji, and others be referred to the proper offices and appointed according to their abilities."

sentences.zh: 東都聞宇文化及西來，上下震懼。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital heard that Yu Wenji was coming west, court and populace alike were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the Eastern Capital that Yu Wenji was marching west, the court and the city were gripped with terror.

sentences.zh: 有蓋琮者，上疏請說李密與之合勢拒化及。

translations.literal: There was one Gai Cong who submitted a memorial asking that Li Mi be persuaded to join forces and resist Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Gai Cong submitted a memorial urging that Li Mi be enlisted to combine forces against Yu Wenji.

sentences.zh: 元文都謂盧楚等曰：「今仇恥未雪而兵力不足，若赦密罪使擊化及，兩賊自鬥，吾徐承其弊。

translations.literal: Yuan Wendu said to Lu Chu and the others: "Today our enemy's shame is not yet avenged and our military strength is insufficient; if we pardon Mi's crimes and have him strike Huaji, the two bandits will fight each other, and we can slowly reap the benefit of their exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wendu told Lu Chu and the others, "Our humiliation is still unavenged and our forces are too weak; if we pardon Li Mi and set him against Yu Wenji, the two enemies will tear at each other while we wait to profit from their exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 化及既破，密兵亦疲；

translations.literal: Once Huaji is broken, Mi's troops will also be weary;
translations.idiomatic: Once Yu Wenji is defeated, Li Mi's army will be spent as well;

sentences.zh: 又其將士利吾官賞，易可離間，並密亦可擒也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, his officers and soldiers will be tempted by our offices and rewards and can easily be set against one another—and Mi too can be captured."
translations.idiomatic: and his officers, lured by our offices and rewards, can readily be turned against him—so Li Mi himself may be taken too."

sentences.zh: 楚等皆以為然，即以琮為通直散騎常侍，繼敕書賜密。

translations.literal: Chu and the others all agreed; Gai Cong was immediately made Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry, and an imperial letter of appointment was sent to bestow on Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chu and the rest agreed, appointed Gai Cong Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry, and dispatched an imperial letter granting Li Mi his commission.

sentences.zh: 丙申，隋信都郡丞東萊麴稜來降，拜冀州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day Bingshen, Qu Ling of Donglai, aide to Xindu commandery under Sui, came to surrender and was appointed prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On Bingshen, Qu Ling of Donglai, deputy magistrate of Sui's Xindu commandery, surrendered and was appointed prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，萬年縣法曹武城孫伏伽上表，以為：「隋以惡聞其過亡天下。

translations.literal: On the day Dingyou, Sun Fuga of Wucheng, legal officer of Wannian county, submitted a memorial, stating: "Sui perished because it hated to hear of its faults.
translations.idiomatic: On Dingyou, Sun Fuga of Wucheng, legal officer of Wannian county, submitted a memorial, saying, "Sui lost the realm because it refused to hear criticism of its failings.

sentences.zh: 陛下龍飛晉陽，遠近響應，未期年而登帝位；

translations.literal: Your Majesty rose like a dragon at Jinyang; near and far responded, and within less than a year you ascended the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rose at Jinyang to widespread acclaim and took the throne in less than a year;

sentences.zh: 徒知得之之易，不知隋失之之不難也。

translations.literal: You know only how easy it was to gain the realm, and do not know how easy it was for Sui to lose it.
translations.idiomatic: you see only how swiftly the throne was won, not how easily Sui lost it.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜易其覆轍，務盡下情。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that you should change that overturned track and strive to exhaust the sentiments of those below.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to avoid Sui's fatal course and make every effort to understand the people's grievances.

sentences.zh: 凡人君言動，不可不慎。

translations.literal: In the words and actions of a ruler, nothing may be treated carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: A sovereign's every word and deed must be weighed with care.

sentences.zh: 竊見陛下今日即位而明日有獻鷂雛者，此乃少年之事，豈聖主所須哉！

translations.literal: Your servant has seen that the day after Your Majesty took the throne, someone presented a young hawk—this is the business of youths; how could a sage ruler need such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: I note that the day after your enthronement someone presented a fledgling hawk—a boy's amusement; what need has a sage ruler of such trifles!

sentences.zh: 又，百戲散樂，亡國淫聲。

translations.literal: Moreover, the hundred entertainments and scattered music are decadent sounds that destroy states.
translations.idiomatic: Again, variety shows and loose music are the licentious sounds that ruin kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 近太常於民間借婦女裙襦五百餘襲以充妓衣，擬五月五日玄武門遊戲，此亦非所以為子孫法也。

translations.literal: Recently the Court of Imperial Sacrifices borrowed more than five hundred women's jackets and skirts from among the people to serve as costumes for entertainers, planning games at the Xuanwu Gate on the fifth day of the fifth month—this too is not a model to bequeath to one's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Court of Imperial Sacrifices borrowed more than five hundred women's jackets and skirts from common households to dress performers for Fifth-of-Fifth festivities at the Xuanwu Gate—hardly an example to set for future generations.

sentences.zh: 凡如此類，悉宜廢罷。

translations.literal: All matters of this kind should entirely be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: All such practices should be abolished at once.

sentences.zh: 善惡之習，朝夕漸染，易以移人。

translations.literal: Habits of good and evil, soaked in day by day, easily shift a person.
translations.idiomatic: Good and bad habits seep in day by day and can swiftly change a man's character.

sentences.zh: 皇太子、諸王參僚左右，宜謹擇其人；

translations.literal: For the Crown Prince and the various princes, the aides and attendants at their sides should be chosen with strict care;
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince and the other princes should have their attendants and advisers chosen with the greatest care;

sentences.zh: 其有門風不能雍睦，為人素無行義，專好奢靡，以聲色遊獵為事者，皆不可使之親近也。

translations.literal: Those whose family conduct cannot achieve harmony, who by nature lack integrity, who devote themselves to extravagance, and who make sensual pleasures, music, and hunting their business—none of these may be allowed to draw near.
translations.idiomatic: anyone from a disorderly household, lacking in moral conduct, devoted to luxury, or given over to pleasure, music, and hunting must be kept far from them.

sentences.zh: 自古及今，骨肉乖離，以至敗國亡家，未有不因左右離間而然也。

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present, when flesh and blood have been estranged, leading to the ruin of states and families, there has never been a case that did not arise from the meddling of those at one's side.
translations.idiomatic: From ancient times to the present, estrangement among kin that brought down houses and kingdoms has always begun with whispering by those at one's elbow.

sentences.zh: 願陛下慎之。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that Your Majesty would be cautious in this."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to guard against this."

sentences.zh: 上省表大悅，下詔褒稱，擢為治書侍御史，賜帛三百匹，仍頒示遠近。

translations.literal: "The Emperor, upon reading the memorial, was greatly pleased; he issued an edict praising it, promoted him to Attendant Imperial Censor, bestowed three hundred bolts of silk, and had it circulated far and near.
translations.idiomatic: "Li Yuan read the memorial with great delight, issued an edict commending it, promoted Sun Fuga to Attendant Imperial Censor, granted him three hundred bolts of silk, and had the edict published throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，內史令延安靖公竇威薨。

translations.literal: On the day Xinchou, Dou Wei, Director of the Secretariat and Duke Jing of Yan'an, died.
translations.idiomatic: On Xinchou, Dou Wei, Director of the Secretariat and Duke Jing of Yan'an, passed away.

sentences.zh: 以將作大匠竇抗兼納言，黃門侍郎陳叔達判納言。

translations.literal: Dou Kang, Master of Palace Construction, was additionally made Chief Counselor; Chen Shuda, Vice Director of the Chancellery, was assigned to adjudicate as Chief Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Kang, Master of Palace Construction, was additionally appointed Chief Counselor, and Chen Shuda, Vice Director of the Chancellery, was assigned to serve concurrently as Chief Counselor.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及留輜重於滑台，以王軌為刑部尚書，使守之，引兵北趣黎陽。

translations.literal: Yu Wenji left baggage trains at Huatai, made Wang Gui Minister of Punishments to guard them, and led troops north toward Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenji left his supply train at Huatai under Wang Gui, whom he appointed Minister of Punishments to guard it, and marched north toward Liyang.

sentences.zh: 李密將徐世勣據黎陽，畏其軍鋒，以兵西保倉城。

translations.literal: Li Mi's general Xu Shiji held Liyang; fearing the enemy's military edge, he withdrew west with troops to defend Cangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi's general Xu Shiji held Liyang but, fearing Yu Wenji's advance, withdrew west to fortify Cangcheng.

sentences.zh: 化及渡河，保黎陽，分兵圍世勣。

translations.literal: Huaji crossed the river, secured Liyang, and divided troops to besiege Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenji crossed the river, occupied Liyang, and sent detachments to besiege Xu Shiji.

sentences.zh: 密帥步騎二萬，壁於清淇，與世勣以烽火相應，深溝高壘，不與化及戰。

translations.literal: Mi led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry, encamped at Qingqi, coordinated with Shiji by signal fires, dug deep ditches and raised high ramparts, and would not give battle to Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi led twenty thousand foot and horse soldiers to encamp at Qingqi, coordinating with Xu Shiji by beacon fire; they dug deep trenches and raised high walls and refused to engage Yu Wenji.

sentences.zh: 化及每攻倉城，密輒引兵以掎其後。

translations.literal: Whenever Huaji attacked Cangcheng, Mi would lead troops to strike his rear.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Yu Wenji assaulted Cangcheng, Li Mi sallied to hit his rear.

sentences.zh: 密與化及隔水而語，密數之曰：「卿本匈奴皁隸破野頭耳，父兄子弟，並受隋恩，富貴累世，舉朝莫二。

translations.literal: Mi and Huaji spoke across the water; Mi reckoned his crimes, saying: "You were originally a black bondservant of the Xiongnu from Poyetu; father, elder brothers, younger brothers, and sons all received Sui's grace, enjoying wealth and honor for generations—unmatched in the whole court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi and Yu Wenji shouted across the water. Li Mi denounced him: "You were nothing but a bondservant of Xiongnu stock from Poyetu; your fathers, brothers, and sons all enjoyed Sui's favor, heaped with wealth and rank for generations—second to none at court.

sentences.zh: 主上失德，不能死諫，反行弒逆，欲規篡奪。

translations.literal: When the sovereign lost virtue, you could not die in remonstrance; instead you carried out regicide, scheming to usurp the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor lost his way, you did not die remonstrating—you murdered him and plotted usurpation.

sentences.zh: 不追諸葛瞻之忠誠，乃為霍禹之惡逆，天地所不容，將欲何之！

translations.literal: You did not follow Zhuge Zhan's loyalty; instead you became a wicked rebel like Huo Yu—intolerable to Heaven and Earth; where do you think you are going!
translations.idiomatic: You did not emulate Zhuge Zhan's loyalty but played the traitor like Huo Yu—Heaven and Earth will not abide you; where do you imagine you can go!

sentences.zh: 若速來歸我，尚可得全後嗣。」

translations.literal: If you quickly come and submit to me, you may yet preserve your descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Surrender to me at once, and your line may yet be spared."

sentences.zh: 化及默然，俯視良久，瞋目大言曰：「與爾論相殺事，何須作書語邪！」

translations.literal: Huaji was silent; he looked down a long while, then glared and shouted: "When I discuss killing with you, what need is there for bookish speech!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenji fell silent, stared downward a long moment, then glared and roared, "We are here to kill each other—why waste breath on pedantry!"

sentences.zh: 密謂從者曰：「化及庸愚如此，忽欲圖為帝王，吾當折杖驅之耳！」

translations.literal: Mi said to those attending him: "Huaji is so base and foolish, yet suddenly he wants to become emperor—I shall break a staff and drive him off!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi told his followers, "Yu Wenji is this dull and stupid, yet he dreams of becoming emperor—I could drive him off with a broken staff!"

sentences.zh: 化及盛修攻具以逼倉城，世勣於城外掘深溝以固守，化及阻塹，不得至城下。

translations.literal: Huaji greatly prepared siege engines to press Cangcheng; Shiji dug deep ditches outside the walls to hold firm, and Huaji was blocked by the trenches and could not reach the foot of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenji built up his siege equipment to press Cangcheng, but Xu Shiji dug deep trenches outside the walls to hold his ground; blocked by the ditches, Yu Wenji could not reach the city wall.

sentences.zh: 世勣於塹中為地道，出兵擊之，化及大敗，焚其攻具。

translations.literal: Shiji made tunnels within the trenches, sent troops out to attack them, Huaji suffered a great defeat, and burned his siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiji dug tunnels beneath the trenches, sortied to strike Yu Wenji's camp, and routed him so thoroughly that Yu Wenji was forced to burn his siege equipment.

sentences.zh: 時密與東都相持日久，又東拒化及，常畏東都議其後。

translations.literal: At that time Mi had been in stalemate with the Eastern Capital for a long time; moreover he held off Huaji to the east and constantly feared the Eastern Capital would move against his rear.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi had long been deadlocked with the Eastern Capital while also blocking Yu Wenji to the east, and he constantly feared that Luoyang might strike at his rear.

sentences.zh: 見蓋琮至，大喜，遂上表乞降，請討滅化及以贖罪，送所獲凶黨雄武郎將於洪建，遣元帥府記室參軍李儉、上開府徐師譽等入見。

translations.literal: When he saw Gai Cong arrive, he was greatly pleased; thereupon he submitted a memorial begging to surrender, requesting permission to attack and destroy Huaji to atone for his crimes, sent the captured villain Xiongwu Commandant Yu Hongjian, and dispatched the marshal's staff recorder Li Jian, Upper Gate Officer Xu Shizhao, and others to audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Gai Cong arrived, Li Mi was overjoyed. He submitted a memorial offering surrender, asked to be allowed to destroy Yu Wenji and thereby redeem his crimes, sent the captured rebel Xiongwu Commandant Yu Hongjian as proof, and dispatched his marshal's staff recorder Li Jian, Upper Gate Officer Xu Shizhao, and others to court.

sentences.zh: 皇泰主命戮洪建於左掖門外，如斛斯政之法。

translations.literal: The Huangtai sovereign ordered Hongjian executed outside the Left Flank Gate, by the method used for Husizheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangtai sovereign ordered Yu Hongjian executed outside the Left Flank Gate, in the same manner as Husizheng had been put to death.

sentences.zh: 元文都等以密降為誠實，盛飾賓館於宣仁門東。

translations.literal: Yuan Wendu and the others regarded Mi's surrender as sincere and lavishly decorated a guest lodge east of Xuanren Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wendu and his faction took Li Mi's surrender at face value and lavishly furnished a guest lodge east of Xuanren Gate.

sentences.zh: 皇泰主引見儉等，以儉為司農卿，師譽為尚書右丞，使具導從，列鐃吹，還館，玉帛酒饌，中使相望。

translations.literal: The Huangtai sovereign received Li Jian and the others in audience, appointed Jian Minister of Agriculture and Shizhao Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, had them fully equipped with escorts, arrayed gongs and horns, and returned them to the lodge; jade, silk, wine, and food were sent in an unbroken stream of palace envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangtai sovereign received Li Jian and his party in audience, named Li Jian Minister of Agriculture and Xu Shizhao Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and sent them back to the lodge with full escort, gongs, and horns while palace envoys arrived in steady succession bearing jade, silk, wine, and feast provisions.

sentences.zh: 冊拜密太尉、尚書令、東南道大行台行軍元帥、魏國公，令先平化及，然後入朝輔政。

translations.literal: Mi was invested by patent as Grand Commandant, Director of the Department of State Affairs, campaign marshal of the Southeast Circuit Grand Commandery, and Duke of Wei, and ordered first to pacify Huaji and only then enter court to assist in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi was formally invested as Grand Commandant, Director of the Department of State Affairs, campaign marshal of the Southeast Circuit Grand Commandery, and Duke of Wei, with orders to subdue Yu Wenji first and only then come to court to assist in government.

sentences.zh: 以徐世勣為右武候大將軍。

translations.literal: Xu Shiji was made Right Martial Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiji was appointed Right Martial Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 仍下詔稱密忠款，且曰：「其用兵機略，一稟魏公節度。」

translations.literal: An edict was also issued praising Mi's loyalty and good faith, saying: "In military strategy and tactics, all shall follow the Duke of Wei's command."
translations.idiomatic: An edict was also issued praising Li Mi's loyalty and sincerity, declaring, "In all military strategy and tactics, command shall rest entirely with the Duke of Wei."

sentences.zh: 元文都等喜於和解，謂天下可定，於上東門置酒作樂，自段達已下皆起舞。

translations.literal: Yuan Wendu and the others rejoiced at the reconciliation, believing the realm could be settled; they set out wine and music at Upper East Gate, and from Duan Da downward all danced.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wendu and his allies rejoiced at the peace with Li Mi and believed the realm was as good as settled. They held a feast with music at Upper East Gate, and from Duan Da on down everyone danced.

sentences.zh: 王世充作色謂起居侍郎崔長文曰：「朝廷官爵，乃以與賊，其志欲何為邪！」

translations.literal: Wang Shichong changed color and said to Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat Cui Changwen: "Court offices and ranks are being given to a bandit—what do they think they are doing!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong's face darkened as he told Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat Cui Changwen, "The court is handing offices and titles to a rebel—what do they imagine they are doing!"

sentences.zh: 文都等亦疑世充欲以城應化及，由是有隙，然猶外相彌縫，陽為親善。

translations.literal: Wendu and the others also suspected Shichong intended to surrender the city to Huaji; because of this there was a rift, yet outwardly they still patched things over and pretended friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wendu and his circle also suspected that Wang Shichong meant to hand the city over to Yu Wenji. From that point a breach opened between them, though outwardly they still patched matters over and feigned goodwill.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，皇泰主遣大理卿張權、鴻臚卿崔善福賜李密書曰：「今日以前，鹹共刷蕩；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Huangtai sovereign sent Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Quan and Director of Ceremonies Cui Shanfu to bestow a letter on Li Mi, saying: "Before today, all alike swept away evil;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the Huangtai sovereign sent Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Quan and Director of Ceremonies Cui Shanfu to deliver a letter to Li Mi that read, "Before today we have all alike swept away evil together;

sentences.zh: 使至以後，彼此通懷。

translations.literal: after your envoys arrive, each side shall open hearts to the other.
translations.idiomatic: from the moment your envoys arrive, let us open our hearts to one another.

sentences.zh: 七政之重，佇公匡弼；

translations.literal: The weight of the seven governances awaits your support and correction;
translations.idiomatic: The weight of state governance awaits your steadying hand;

sentences.zh: 九伐之利，委公指揮。」

translations.literal: the advantage of the nine punitive campaigns is entrusted to your command."
translations.idiomatic: the power of punitive campaigns is entrusted entirely to your command."

sentences.zh: 權等既至，密北面拜受詔書。

translations.literal: When Quan and the others arrived, Mi faced north, bowed, and received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Quan and his party arrived, Li Mi turned north, bowed, and received the imperial letter.

sentences.zh: 既無西慮，悉以精兵東擊化及。

translations.literal: Having no further concern on the western front, he sent all his elite troops east to attack Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: With no further worry about his western flank, he committed all his best troops to an eastern campaign against Yu Wenji.

sentences.zh: 密知化及軍糧且盡，因偽與和；

translations.literal: Mi knew Huaji's army provisions were nearly exhausted and therefore feigned making peace with him;
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi knew Yu Wenji's army was running out of grain and therefore pretended to negotiate peace;

sentences.zh: 化及大喜，恣其兵食，冀密饋之。

translations.literal: Huaji was greatly pleased, let his soldiers eat freely, and hoped Mi would supply him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenji was delighted, let his men eat freely, and hoped Li Mi would feed his army.

sentences.zh: 會密下有人獲罪，亡抵化及，具言其情，化及大怒；

translations.literal: It happened that someone under Mi who had been punished fled to Huaji and fully explained the situation; Huaji was greatly enraged;
translations.idiomatic: Just then a man under Li Mi who had been punished fled to Yu Wenji and told him the whole scheme; Yu Wenji flew into a rage;

sentences.zh: 其食又盡，乃渡永濟渠，與密戰於童山之下，自辰達酉；

translations.literal: his food was again exhausted, so he crossed the Yongji Canal and fought Mi below Mount Tong, from the hour Chen until the hour You;
translations.idiomatic: his provisions were again exhausted, so he crossed the Yongji Canal and fought Li Mi below Mount Tong from morning until evening;

sentences.zh: 密為流矢所中，墮馬悶絕，左右奔散。

translations.literal: Mi was struck by a stray arrow, fell from his horse in a faint, and those around him fled in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi was struck by a stray arrow, fell from his horse unconscious, and his attendants scattered.

sentences.zh: 追兵且至，唯秦叔寶獨捍衛之，密由是獲免。

translations.literal: Pursuing troops were about to arrive; only Qin Shubao alone defended him, and Mi thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers were closing in, but Qin Shubao alone held them off, and Li Mi escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 叔寶復收兵與之力戰，化及乃退。

translations.literal: Shubao again gathered troops and fought him fiercely, and Huaji then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shubao rallied his men and fought on until Yu Wenji finally withdrew.

sentences.zh: 化及入汲郡求軍糧，又遣使拷掠東郡吏民以責米粟。

translations.literal: Huaji entered Ji Commandery to seek army provisions and also sent envoys to torture and plunder the officials and people of Dong Commandery to demand grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenji entered Ji Commandery in search of army grain and sent envoys to torture and plunder the officials and people of Dong Commandery to extort rice and millet.

sentences.zh: 王軌等不堪其弊，遣通事舍人許敬宗詣密請降；

translations.literal: Wang Gui and the others could not endure the suffering and sent Palace Secretariat Attendant Xu Jingzong to Mi to request surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui and his men could no longer endure the abuse and sent Palace Secretariat Attendant Xu Jingzong to Li Mi to offer surrender;

sentences.zh: 密以軌為滑州總管，以敬宗為元帥府記室，與魏徵共掌文翰。

translations.literal: Mi made Gui overall commander of Huazhou and Jingzong staff recorder of the marshal's headquarters, sharing charge of documents with Wei Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi appointed Wang Gui overall commander of Huazhou and Xu Jingzong staff recorder of his marshal's headquarters, where Xu Jingzong shared charge of documents with Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 敬宗，善心之子也。

translations.literal: Jingzong was the son of Shanxin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong was the son of Xu Shanxin.

sentences.zh: 房公蘇威在東郡，隨眾降密，密以其隋氏大臣，虛心禮之。

translations.literal: Lord Fang Su Wei was in Dong Commandery; he followed the crowd in surrendering to Mi, and Mi, because he was a great minister of the Sui house, received him with humble courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Fang Su Wei was in Dong Commandery and surrendered to Li Mi along with the rest. Because he was a senior minister of the Sui house, Li Mi received him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 威見密，初不言帝室艱危，唯再三舞蹈，稱「不圖今日復睹聖明！」

translations.literal: When Wei saw Mi, at first he did not speak of the imperial house's peril; he only danced repeatedly in obeisance, saying, "I never dreamed I would again behold such sagely brilliance today!"
translations.idiomatic: When Su Wei met Li Mi, he said nothing at first about the peril facing the imperial house; he only bowed again and again, exclaiming, "I never dreamed I would again behold such sagely brilliance today!"

sentences.zh: 時人鄙之。

translations.literal: People of the time despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 化及聞王軌叛，大懼，自汲郡引兵欲取以北諸郡，其將陳智略帥嶺南驍果萬餘人，樊文超帥江淮排，張童兒帥江東驍果數千人，皆降於密。

translations.literal: When Huaji heard that Wang Gui had rebelled, he was greatly afraid; he led troops out from Ji Commandery intending to seize the commanderies north of the Yellow River. His generals Chen Zhilue led more than ten thousand fierce soldiers from Lingnan, Fan Wenchao led Jianghuai pike troops, and Zhang Tong'er led several thousand fierce soldiers from Jiangdong—all surrendered to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Wenji learned that Wang Gui had defected, he was terrified. He marched out of Ji Commandery intending to seize the commanderies north of the Yellow River, but his generals Chen Zhilue with more than ten thousand Lingnan shock troops, Fan Wenchao with Jianghuai pike corps, and Zhang Tong'er with several thousand Jiangdong shock troops all surrendered to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 文超，子蓋之子也。

translations.literal: Wenchao was the son of Zigai.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wenchao was the son of Fan Zigai.

sentences.zh: 化及猶有眾二萬，北趣魏縣；

translations.literal: Huaji still had a force of twenty thousand and marched north toward Wei County;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenji still had twenty thousand men and marched north toward Wei County;

sentences.zh: 密知其無能為，西還鞏洛，留徐世勣以備之。

translations.literal: Mi knew he could do nothing further, returned west to Gong and Luoyang, and left Xu Shiji to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi knew Yu Wenji was finished, withdrew west to the Gong-Luoyang region, and left Xu Shiji to keep watch on him.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，宣州刺史周超擊朱粲，敗之。

translations.literal: On the day Yisi, Xu Prefecture Inspector Zhou Chao attacked Zhu Can and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On Yisi, Xu Prefecture Inspector Zhou Chao attacked Zhu Can and routed him.

sentences.zh: 丁未，梁師都寇靈州，驃騎將軍藺興粲擊破之。

translations.literal: On the day Dingwei, Liang Shidu raided Lingzhou; Flying Cavalry General Lin Xingcan attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On Dingwei, Liang Shidu raided Lingzhou and was beaten back by Flying Cavalry General Lin Xingcan.

sentences.zh: 突厥闕可汗遣使內附。

translations.literal: Que Khan of the Turks sent envoys to submit internally.
translations.idiomatic: Que Khan of the Turks sent envoys to offer submission to the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 初，闕可汗附於李軌；

translations.literal: Initially Que Khan had attached himself to Li Gui;
translations.idiomatic: At first Que Khan had allied himself with Li Gui;

sentences.zh: 隋西戎使者曹瓊據甘州誘之，乃更附瓊，與之拒軌；

translations.literal: the Sui Western Regions envoy Cao Qiong, holding Ganzhou, enticed him, whereupon he attached himself instead to Qiong and with him resisted Gui;
translations.idiomatic: then the Sui Western Regions envoy Cao Qiong, who held Ganzhou, lured him away, and Que Khan switched allegiance to Cao Qiong and joined him in resisting Li Gui;

sentences.zh: 為軌所敗，竄於達斗拔谷，與吐谷渾相表裡，至是內附，上厚加慰撫。

translations.literal: He was defeated by Gui, fled into Dadou Bagu Valley, acted in concert with Tuyuhun inside and out, and at this time submitted internally; the sovereign richly rewarded and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui defeated him, and he fled into Dadou Bagu Valley, where he coordinated with Tuyuhun in a pincer arrangement. Now he submitted to the Tang court, and the sovereign treated him with generous reassurance.

sentences.zh: 尋為李軌所滅。

translations.literal: Before long he was destroyed by Li Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Gui destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 薛舉進逼高址，遊兵至於豳、岐，秦王世民深溝高壘不與戰。

translations.literal: Xue Ju pressed close to Gaozhi; raiding troops reached Bin and Qi; the Prince of Qin Shimin dug deep ditches and raised high ramparts and would not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju pressed toward Gaozhi, and his raiders reached as far as Bin and Qi. The Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, dug deep trenches, raised high walls, and refused to fight.

sentences.zh: 會世民得瘧疾，委軍事於長史、納言劉文靜、司馬殷開山，且戒之曰：「薛舉懸軍深入，食少兵疲，若來挑戰，慎勿應也。

translations.literal: It happened that Shimin contracted malaria; he entrusted military affairs to Chief Administrator and Chief Counselor Liu Wenjing and Vice Director Yin Kaishan, and admonished them, saying: "Xue Ju has led his army deep on a distant campaign with little food and weary troops; if they come to provoke battle, be careful not to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Li Shimin came down with malaria and entrusted military affairs to Chief Administrator and Chief Counselor Liu Wenjing and Vice Director Yin Kaishan, warning them, "Xue Ju has marched deep with little food and weary troops. If they come to provoke a fight, do not respond.

sentences.zh: 俟吾疾愈，為君等破之。」

translations.literal: Wait until my illness is cured, and I will break them for you."
translations.idiomatic: Wait until I recover, and I will break them for you."

sentences.zh: 開山退，謂文靜曰：「王慮公不能辦，故有此言耳。

translations.literal: Kaishan withdrew and said to Wenjing: "The prince thinks we cannot manage it, and therefore spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Kaishan withdrew and told Liu Wenjing, "The prince thinks we cannot handle this—that is why he said what he did.

sentences.zh: 且賊聞王有疾，必輕我，宜曜武以威之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, when the bandits hear the prince is ill, they are sure to despise us; we should display martial prowess to overawe them."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, once the enemy hears the prince is ill, they are bound to look down on us. We ought to display our strength and overawe them."

sentences.zh: 乃陳於高址西南，恃眾而不設備。

translations.literal: Thereupon they deployed southwest of Gaozhi, relying on their numbers and making no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: They then deployed southwest of Gaozhi, confident in their numbers and taking no precautions.

sentences.zh: 舉潛師掩其後，壬子，戰於淺水原，八總管皆敗，士卒死者什五六，大將軍慕容羅□、李安遠、劉弘基皆沒，世民引兵還長安。

translations.literal: Ju sent troops secretly to strike their rear; on the day Renzi they fought at Qianshui Plain; all eight overall commanders were defeated, and fifteen or sixteen out of every ten soldiers died; Grand Generals Murong Luohou, Li Anyuan, and Liu Hongji all fell in the field; Shimin led troops back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju sent a hidden force to fall on their rear. On Renzi they fought at Qianshui Plain. All eight overall commanders were routed, and fifteen or sixteen men in every hundred were killed. Grand Generals Murong Luohou, Li Anyuan, and Liu Hongji were all captured or killed, and Li Shimin withdrew to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 舉遂拔高址，收唐兵死者為京觀；

translations.literal: Ju thereupon took Gaozhi, gathered the dead Tang soldiers into a victory mound;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju then took Gaozhi and piled the dead Tang soldiers into a victory mound;

sentences.zh: 文靜等皆坐除名。

translations.literal: Wenjing and the others were all punished by removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenjing and the others were all stripped of their posts.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，榆林賊帥郭子和遣使來降。

translations.literal: On the day Yimao, the bandit chieftain of Yulin Guo Zihe sent envoys to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On Yimao, Guo Zihe, the bandit chieftain of Yulin, sent envoys to surrender.

sentences.zh: 以為靈州總管。

translations.literal: He was made overall commander of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed overall commander of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 李密每戰勝，輒遣使告捷於皇泰主。

translations.literal: Each time Li Mi won a battle, he would send envoys to report victory to the Huangtai sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Li Mi won a battle, he sent envoys to report the victory to the Huangtai sovereign.

sentences.zh: 隋人皆喜，王世充獨謂其麾下曰：「元文都輩，刀筆吏耳，吾觀其勢，必為李密所擒。

translations.literal: Sui loyalists were all pleased; Wang Shichong alone said to his followers: "Yuan Wendu and his sort are mere clerks with pens and knives; I observe their situation—they are sure to be captured by Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Sui loyalists rejoiced, but Wang Shichong alone told his followers, "Yuan Wendu and his crowd are nothing but clerks with pens and knives. I can see how this ends—they will be taken by Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 且吾軍士屢與密戰，沒其父兄子弟，前後已多，一旦為之下，吾屬無類矣！」

translations.literal: Moreover our soldiers have repeatedly fought Mi, losing fathers, elder brothers, and younger kinsmen—many already, front and back; if we suddenly fall under him, none of us will survive!"
