translations.idiomatic: Our soldiers have fought Li Mi again and again and lost fathers, brothers, and sons—many of them. If we suddenly submit to him, none of us will be left alive!"

sentences.zh: 欲以激怒其眾。

translations.literal: He intended thereby to enrage his troops.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to inflame his troops with these words.

sentences.zh: 文都聞之，大懼，與盧楚等謀因世充入朝，伏甲誅之。

translations.literal: When Wendu heard this, he was greatly afraid; with Lu Chu and others he plotted that when Shichong entered court, hidden soldiers would kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Wendu heard this, he was terrified and plotted with Lu Chu and others to ambush and kill Wang Shichong when he came to court.

sentences.zh: 段達性庸懦，恐事不就，遣其婿張志以楚等謀告世充。

translations.literal: Duan Da was by nature mediocre and timid; fearing the affair would not succeed, he sent his son-in-law Zhang Zhi to inform Shichong of Chu and the others' plot.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da was timid by nature and, fearing the plot would fail, sent his son-in-law Zhang Zhi to warn Wang Shichong of Lu Chu and the others' scheme.

sentences.zh: 戊午夜三鼓，世充勒兵襲含嘉門。

translations.literal: On the night of Wuwu, at the third watch, Shichong mustered troops and struck Hanjia Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of Wuwu, at the third watch, Wang Shichong mustered his troops and stormed Hanjia Gate.

sentences.zh: 元文都聞變，入奉皇泰主御乾陽殿，陳兵自衛，命諸將閉門拒守。

translations.literal: When Yuan Wendu heard of the disturbance, he entered to attend the Huangtai sovereign at Qianyang Hall, arrayed troops for self-defense, and ordered the generals to shut the gates and hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Wendu heard of the coup, he rushed to escort the Huangtai sovereign to Qianyang Hall, drew up troops to defend him, and ordered the generals to shut the gates and hold the palace.

sentences.zh: 將軍跋野綱將兵出，遇世充，下馬降之。

translations.literal: General Baye Gang led troops out, encountered Shichong, dismounted, and surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: General Baye Gang marched out with troops, met Wang Shichong, dismounted, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 將軍費曜、田闍戰於門外，不利。

translations.literal: Generals Fei Yao and Tian Chan fought outside the gate and fared badly.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Fei Yao and Tian Chan fought outside the gate and were driven back.

sentences.zh: 文都自將宿衛兵欲出玄武門以襲其後，長秋監段瑜稱求門鑰不獲，稽留遂久。

translations.literal: Wendu personally led the palace guard troops intending to go out through Xuanwu Gate to strike their rear; Chief of the Long Autumn Office Duan Yu claimed he could not obtain the gate keys, and the delay dragged on.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wendu personally led the palace guard, intending to sally from Xuanwu Gate and hit Wang Shichong from the rear, but Chief of the Long Autumn Office Duan Yu claimed he could not get the gate keys, and the delay dragged on.

sentences.zh: 天且曙，文都引兵復欲出太陽門逆戰，還至乾陽殿，世充已攻太陽門得入。

translations.literal: Dawn was near; Wendu led troops intending again to go out through Taiyang Gate to meet the enemy in battle; when he returned to Qianyang Hall, Shichong had already assaulted Taiyang Gate and gained entry.
translations.idiomatic: As dawn approached, Yuan Wendu tried again to march out through Taiyang Gate to meet the attack, but by the time he returned to Qianyang Hall, Wang Shichong had already forced Taiyang Gate and entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 皇甫無逸棄母及妻子，斫右掖門，西奔長安。

translations.literal: Huangfu Wuyi abandoned his mother and wife and children, hacked through the Right Flank Gate, and fled west to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Wuyi abandoned his mother, wife, and children, hacked through the Right Flank Gate, and fled west to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 盧楚匿於太官署，世充之黨擒之，至興教門，見世充，世充令亂斬殺之；

translations.literal: Lu Chu hid in the Grand Provisioner's Office; Shichong's partisans seized him; when he reached Xingjiao Gate and saw Shichong, Shichong ordered him hacked to death;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chu hid in the Grand Provisioner's Office, but Wang Shichong's men seized him. At Xingjiao Gate he was brought before Wang Shichong, who ordered him hacked to death;

sentences.zh: 進攻紫微宮門。

translations.literal: then pressed the attack on the Ziwei Palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: then pressed the attack on the Ziwei Palace gate.

sentences.zh: 皇泰主使人登紫微觀。

translations.literal: The Huangtai sovereign sent someone up to Ziwei Tower.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangtai sovereign sent a messenger up to Ziwei Tower.

sentences.zh: 問：「稱兵欲何為？」

translations.literal: He asked: "You have raised troops—what do you intend?"
translations.idiomatic: He called down, "You have raised troops—what do you intend?"

sentences.zh: 世充下馬謝曰：「元文都、盧楚等橫見規圖；

translations.literal: Shichong dismounted and apologized, saying: "Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, and the others plotted against me without cause;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong dismounted and apologized, saying, "Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, and the others plotted against me without cause;

sentences.zh: 請殺文都，甘從刑典。」

translations.literal: I ask that Wendu be killed; I willingly submit to the penal code."
translations.idiomatic: kill Yuan Wendu, and I will willingly submit to the law."

sentences.zh: 段達乃令將軍黃桃樹執送文都。

translations.literal: Duan Da then ordered General Huang Taoshu to seize and deliver Wendu.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da then ordered General Huang Taoshu to seize Yuan Wendu and bring him forward.

sentences.zh: 文都顧謂皇泰主曰：「臣今朝死，陛下夕及矣！」

translations.literal: Wendu turned and said to the Huangtai sovereign: "If your servant dies this morning, Your Majesty will follow this evening!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wendu turned to the Huangtai sovereign and said, "If I die this morning, Your Majesty will follow this evening!"

sentences.zh: 皇泰主慟哭遣之，出興教門，亂斬如盧楚，並殺盧、元諸子。

translations.literal: The Huangtai sovereign wept bitterly as he sent him away; outside Xingjiao Gate he was hacked to death like Lu Chu, and the sons of Lu and Yuan were all killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangtai sovereign wept as he sent him away. Outside Xingjiao Gate Yuan Wendu was hacked to death like Lu Chu, and the sons of the Lu and Yuan families were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 段達又以皇泰主命開門納世充，世充悉遣人代宿衛者，然後入見皇泰主於乾陽殿。

translations.literal: Duan Da again, by the Huangtai sovereign's order, opened the gate and admitted Shichong; Shichong sent men to replace all the palace guards, and only then entered to see the Huangtai sovereign at Qianyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da then, by the Huangtai sovereign's order, opened the gates and admitted Wang Shichong, who replaced every palace guardsman with his own men before entering to see the Huangtai sovereign at Qianyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 皇泰主謂世充曰：「擅相誅殺，曾不聞奏，豈為臣之道乎！

translations.literal: The Huangtai sovereign said to Shichong: "You killed people on your own authority without ever reporting it— is this the way of a minister!
translations.idiomatic: The Huangtai sovereign said to Wang Shichong, "You killed men on your own authority without ever reporting it—is this the conduct of a loyal minister!

sentences.zh: 公欲肆其強力，敢及我邪！」

translations.literal: You wish to unleash your brute force—dare you reach even to me!"
translations.idiomatic: Do you mean to unleash your brute force even against me!"

sentences.zh: 世充拜伏流涕謝曰：「臣蒙先皇采拔，粉骨非報。

translations.literal: Shichong bowed prostrate, weeping, and apologized, saying: "Your servant received selection and promotion from the late emperor; grinding my bones to powder would not repay the debt.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong prostrated himself, weeping, and apologized, "Your servant was raised up by the late emperor; I could grind my bones to powder and still not repay that debt.

sentences.zh: 文都等苞藏禍心，欲召李密以危社稷，疾臣違異，深積猜嫌；

translations.literal: Wendu and the others harbored evil intent, wishing to summon Li Mi to endanger the altars of state; they resented my dissent and deeply accumulated suspicion;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wendu and his faction harbored evil intent and meant to summon Li Mi to endanger the throne. They resented my opposition and nursed deep suspicions against me;

sentences.zh: 臣迫於救死，不暇聞奏。

translations.literal: your servant was forced to save his life and had no leisure to report to court.
translations.idiomatic: I was forced to save my own life and had no time to report to court.

sentences.zh: 若內懷不臧，違負陛下，天地日月，實所照臨，使臣闔門殄滅，無復遺類。」

translations.literal: If within I harbor evil and betray Your Majesty, may Heaven and Earth and sun and moon, which truly look down upon all, cause my whole household to be exterminated without a survivor."
translations.idiomatic: If I harbor evil in my heart and betray Your Majesty, may Heaven and Earth and sun and moon, which look down upon all, destroy my whole house without a survivor."

sentences.zh: 詞淚俱發。

translations.literal: Words and tears issued together.
translations.idiomatic: His words and tears came together.

sentences.zh: 皇泰主以為誠，引令升殿，與語久之，因與俱入見皇太后；

translations.literal: The Huangtai sovereign believed him sincere, had him ascend the hall, spoke with him a long while, and then went together with him to see the Empress Dowager;
translations.idiomatic: The Huangtai sovereign took him at his word, had him ascend the hall, and spoke with him at length before going together to see the Empress Dowager;

sentences.zh: 世充被發為誓，稱不敢有貳心。

translations.literal: Shichong bared his head to swear an oath, declaring he dared not harbor a second heart.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong bared his head to swear an oath that he would never harbor disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 乃以世充為左僕射、總督內外諸軍事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shichong was made Left Vice Director and overall commander of all internal and external military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong was then appointed Left Vice Director and overall commander of all internal and external military affairs.

sentences.zh: 比及日中，捕獲趙長文、郭文懿，殺之。

translations.literal: By midday Zhao Changwen and Guo Wenyi were captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: By midday Zhao Changwen and Guo Wenyi were captured and killed.

sentences.zh: 然後巡城，告諭以誅元、盧之意。

translations.literal: Only then did he patrol the city, announcing and instructing the people regarding his intent in executing Yuan and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He then toured the city and announced that he had killed Yuan Wendu and Lu Chu.

sentences.zh: 世充自含嘉城移居尚書省，漸結黨援，恣行威福。

translations.literal: Shichong moved from Hanjia City to the Department of State Affairs, gradually built up a factional network, and exercised authority and favor as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong moved from Hanjia City into the Department of State Affairs, gradually built a factional network, and wielded power and favor as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 用兄世惲為內史令，入居禁中，子弟鹹典兵馬，分政事為十頭，悉以其黨主之，勢震內外，莫不趨附，皇泰主拱手而已。

translations.literal: He employed his elder brother Shiyun as Director of the Secretariat, who entered and dwelt within the forbidden precincts; younger kinsmen all held command of troops and horses; he divided governance into ten bureaus and put his partisans in charge of all of them; his power shook inner and outer court, and none failed to rush to attach themselves—the Huangtai sovereign could only fold his hands.
translations.idiomatic: He installed his elder brother Wang Shiyun as Director of the Secretariat inside the palace, placed younger kinsmen in command of troops, divided government into ten bureaus staffed entirely with his partisans, and built a power that shook the court. Everyone rushed to attach themselves to him, and the Huangtai sovereign could only fold his hands.

sentences.zh: 李密將入朝，至溫，聞元文都等死，乃還金墉。

translations.literal: Li Mi was about to enter court; when he reached Wen, he heard that Yuan Wendu and the others were dead, and thereupon returned to Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi was on his way to court when he reached Wen and learned that Yuan Wendu and his allies were dead; he turned back to Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 東都大饑，私錢濫惡，太半雜以錫環，其細如線，米斛直錢八九萬。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital suffered great famine; private coin was debased and bad, more than half mixed with tin rings as fine as thread; a hu of rice cost eighty or ninety thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital was in the grip of famine. Private coin was debased, more than half of it tin rings as fine as thread, and a hu of rice cost eighty or ninety thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 初，李密嘗受業於儒生徐文遠。

translations.literal: Initially Li Mi had once studied under the Confucian scholar Xu Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi had once studied under the Confucian scholar Xu Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 文遠為皇泰主國子祭酒，自出樵采，為密軍所執；

translations.literal: Wenyuan was Grand Master of the National University for the Huangtai sovereign; he went out himself to gather firewood and was seized by Mi's army;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wenyuan served the Huangtai sovereign as Grand Master of the National University. He went out to gather firewood himself and was seized by Li Mi's troops;

sentences.zh: 密令文遠南面坐，備弟子禮，北面拜之。

translations.literal: Mi had Wenyuan sit facing south, prepared the rites due a teacher, and bowed to him facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi had Xu Wenyuan seated facing south, treated him with the full courtesy due a teacher, and bowed to him facing north.

sentences.zh: 文遠曰：「老夫既荷厚禮，敢不盡言！

translations.literal: Wenyuan said: "This old man, having received such generous courtesy, dares not hold back his words!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wenyuan said, "Since you have honored me so generously, this old man dares not hold back!

sentences.zh: 未審將軍之志欲為伊、霍以繼絕扶傾乎？

translations.literal: I do not yet know whether the general's intent is to be an Yi or Huo, continuing the broken line and supporting what is toppling?
translations.idiomatic: Tell me, General—do you mean to be an Yi Yin or a Huo Guang, restoring a broken line and propping up a falling house?

sentences.zh: 則老夫雖遲暮，猶願盡力；

translations.literal: If so, then though this old man is in his late years, he still wishes to exert his utmost strength;
translations.idiomatic: If that is your aim, then though I am old, I am still willing to give you my best;

sentences.zh: 若為莽、卓，乘危邀利，則無所用老夫矣！」

translations.literal: If you were like Wang Mang or Dong Zhuo, seizing crisis to pursue profit, then this old man would be of no use to you!"
translations.idiomatic: If you were another Wang Mang or Dong Zhuo, seizing crisis for profit, you would have no use for this old man!"

sentences.zh: 密頓首曰：「昨奉朝命，備位上公，冀竭庸虛，匡濟國難，此密之本志也。」

translations.literal: Mi bowed his head to the ground and said: "Yesterday I received the court's command and took the rank of supreme duke, hoping to exhaust my feeble powers to rescue the state's calamity—this has been Mi's original resolve."
translations.idiomatic: Mi bowed low and said, "Yesterday I received the court's command and took the rank of supreme duke, hoping to exhaust my feeble powers to rescue the state from calamity—that has always been my purpose."

sentences.zh: 文遠曰：「將軍名臣之子，失塗至此，若能不遠而復，猶不失為忠義之臣。」

translations.literal: Wenyuan said: "General, you are the son of a famous minister who has strayed to this pass; if you can turn back before you go too far, you may still not fail to be a loyal and righteous subject."
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan said, "General, you are the son of a famous minister who has lost his way. If you can turn back before you go too far, you may still prove a loyal subject."

sentences.zh: 及王世充殺元文都等，密復問計於文遠。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong killed Yuan Wendu and the others, Mi again asked Wenyuan for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong killed Yuan Wendu and the others, Mi again sought Wenyuan's counsel.

sentences.zh: 文遠曰：「世充亦門人也，其為人殘忍褊隘，既乘此勢，必有異圖，將軍前計為不諧矣。

translations.literal: Wenyuan said: "Shichong is also a follower of your school; by nature he is cruel and narrow-minded. Now that he has seized this momentum, he is sure to harbor other designs—your former plan will not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan said, "Shichong is also your follower, but he is cruel and narrow-minded. Having seized this momentum, he is sure to harbor other designs—your former plan will not work.

sentences.zh: 非破世充，不可入朝也。」

translations.literal: Unless Shichong is defeated, you cannot enter court."
translations.idiomatic: Unless you defeat Shichong, you cannot go to court."

sentences.zh: 密曰：「始謂先生儒者，不達時事，今乃坐決大計，何其明也！」

translations.literal: Mi said: "At first I thought you, sir, were a Confucian scholar who did not understand current affairs; now you settle great strategy from your seat—how clear-sighted you are!"
translations.idiomatic: Mi said, "At first I thought you were a scholar out of touch with affairs. Now you settle great strategy from your seat—how clear-sighted you are!"

sentences.zh: 文遠，孝嗣之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Wenyuan was the great-great-grandson of Xiao Xiaosi.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan was the great-great-grandson of Xiao Xiaosi.

sentences.zh: 庚申，詔隋氏離宮游幸之所並廢之。

translations.literal: On the day Gengshen an edict ordered that all the Sui dynasty's detached palaces and touring residences be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengshen an edict abolished all the Sui dynasty's detached palaces and touring residences.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，遣黃台公瑗安撫山南。

translations.literal: On the day Wuchen the Duke of Huangtai Yuan was sent to pacify and reassure the southern mountains region.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuchen the Duke of Huangtai Li Yuan was dispatched to pacify the southern mountains region.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以隋右武衛將軍皇甫無逸為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: On the day Jisi the Sui Right Martial Guard general Huangfu Wuyi was appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jisi former Sui Right Martial Guard general Huangfu Wuyi was appointed Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 隋河間郡丞王琮守郡城以拒群盜，竇建德攻之，歲餘不下；

translations.literal: Sui Hejian commandery aide Wang Cong held the commandery city to resist the bandit hosts; Dou Jiande attacked it for more than a year without taking it;
translations.idiomatic: Sui Hejian commandery aide Wang Cong held the city against the bandits; Dou Jiande besieged it for more than a year without success;

sentences.zh: 聞煬帝凶問，帥吏士發喪，乘城者皆哭。

translations.literal: when news of Emperor Yang's violent death arrived, he led officials and soldiers in mourning rites, and all upon the walls wept.
translations.idiomatic: when news of Emperor Yang's death arrived, he led officials and soldiers in mourning, and everyone on the walls wept.

sentences.zh: 建德遣使吊之，琮因使者請降，建德退捨具饌以待之。

translations.literal: Jiande sent envoys to offer condolences; Cong used the envoys to request surrender, and Jiande withdrew his camp, prepared food and drink, and awaited him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande sent envoys to offer condolences. Cong used them to request surrender, and Jiande withdrew his camp, prepared a feast, and awaited him.

sentences.zh: 琮言及隋亡，俯伏流涕，建德亦為之泣。

translations.literal: When Cong spoke of the fall of Sui he prostrated himself and wept; Jiande wept for it as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong spoke of Sui's fall he prostrated himself and wept; Jiande wept with him.

sentences.zh: 諸將曰：「琮久拒我軍，殺傷甚眾，力盡乃降，請烹之。」

translations.literal: The generals said: "Cong long resisted our army and killed and wounded many of our men; he surrendered only when his strength was spent—please boil him alive."
translations.idiomatic: The generals said, "Cong long resisted us and killed many of our men. He surrendered only when exhausted—boil him alive."

sentences.zh: 建德曰：「琮，忠臣也，吾方賞之以勸事君，奈何殺之！

translations.literal: Jiande said: "Cong is a loyal minister; I am just about to reward him to encourage service to one's lord—how can we kill him!
translations.idiomatic: Jiande said, "Cong is a loyal minister. I mean to reward him to encourage loyalty—how can we kill him!

sentences.zh: 往在高雞泊為盜，容可妄殺人；

translations.literal: In the past at Gaojipo we were bandits and might kill people recklessly;
translations.idiomatic: When we were bandits at Gaojipo we might kill recklessly;

sentences.zh: 今欲安百姓，定天下，豈得害忠良乎！」

translations.literal: now we wish to settle the people and pacify the realm—how can we harm the loyal and good!"
translations.idiomatic: but now we wish to settle the people and pacify the realm—how can we harm the loyal and good!"

sentences.zh: 乃徇軍中曰：「先與王琮有怨敢妄動者，夷三族！」

translations.literal: He thereupon proclaimed through the army: "Whoever had prior grievance with Wang Cong and dares act rashly—his three clans shall be exterminated!"
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed through the army, "Anyone who had a prior grievance with Wang Cong and dares act against him—his three clans shall be exterminated!"

sentences.zh: 以琮為瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: He appointed Cong prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Cong prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是河北郡縣聞之，爭附於建德。

translations.literal: Thereupon the commanderies and counties of Hebei, hearing of this, vied to attach themselves to Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon commanderies and counties throughout Hebei, hearing of this, rushed to submit to Jiande.

sentences.zh: 先是，建德陷景城，執戶曹河東張玄素，將殺之，縣民千餘人號泣請代其死，曰：「戶曹清慎無比，大王殺之，何以勸善！」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jiande took Jingcheng he seized household registrar Zhang Xuansu of Hedong and was about to kill him; more than a thousand county people wailed and begged to die in his place, saying: "The household registrar is matchless in integrity and caution—if Your Majesty kills him, how will you encourage goodness!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jiande took Jingcheng he seized household registrar Zhang Xuansu of Hedong and was about to kill him. More than a thousand townspeople wailed and begged to die in his place, saying, "The household registrar is matchless in integrity—if you kill him, how will you encourage goodness!"

sentences.zh: 建德乃釋之，以為治書侍御史，固辭；

translations.literal: Jiande thereupon released him and wished to make him attendant censor for drafting documents, but Xuansu firmly declined;
translations.idiomatic: Jiande released him and offered him the post of attendant censor for drafting documents, but Xuansu firmly declined;

sentences.zh: 及江都敗，復以為黃門侍郎，玄素乃起。

translations.literal: when Jiangdu fell he again offered him Yellow Gate vice director, and only then did Xuansu accept.
translations.idiomatic: when Jiangdu fell he again offered him Yellow Gate vice director, and only then did Xuansu accept.

sentences.zh: 饒陽令宋正本，博學有才氣，說建德以定河北之策，建德引為謀主。

translations.literal: Raoyang magistrate Song Zhengben, learned and talented, urged upon Jiande a strategy to settle Hebei; Jiande took him as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Raoyang magistrate Song Zhengben, learned and talented, urged a strategy to settle Hebei upon Jiande, who took him as chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 建德定都樂壽，命所居曰金城宮，備置百官。

translations.literal: Jiande made Leshou his capital, named his residence Golden City Palace, and fully established the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande made Leshou his capital, named his residence Golden City Palace, and established a full bureaucracy.
